# Condition recovery and exposure — provisional procedures

**Reviewed provisional integration, 8 October 2026.** These are fictional game procedures. The sources provide the condition identities, existing dose/tolerance rules, six Exhaustion levels and Intoxication thresholds; the exact generic recovery projects and missing endpoints below are newly authored proposals discussed with GPT. Preserve the original sources. Use with [all 28 conditions](CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md) and [HP, Wounds and death](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md).

## Time, costs and checks

A project day is a consecutive 24-hour interval starting when that project begins, not a calendar-date change. A three-day project finishes no earlier than 72 elapsed hours; seven days means at least 168 hours. Only one project of the same kind for the same patient and named condition may be active. Concurrent clocks measure the same elapsed time once; the same active hour or consumed Supply cannot pay two activities. An active practitioner cannot simultaneously perform a long rest. A patient can receive care while resting where the care permits it.

Consume each stated Supply or kit use at the beginning of its attempt or daily work. Interruption does not refund it. Missing a required project day, taking a forbidden dose or receiving forbidden new Exposure ends that attempt; completed costs remain spent, and starting again requires a fresh full project. Merely suppressing symptoms does not interrupt abstinence or time already properly completed.

Project skill checks use the reviewed four-degree task rules. Success and Critical Success give the stated success; Failure and Critical Failure give the stated failure unless specifically differentiated. No extra reward or complication is inferred from an undefined degree. Saving throws remain binary. Use WIS (Medicine), INT (Religion), INT (Arcana), or an INT check using proficiency with alchemist's supplies for Alchemy. These ability/tool assignments are explicit integration choices; an actual feature can supply its printed alternative.

## Exhaustion

The six V6 effects are cumulative: level 1 disadvantage on ability checks; 2 Speed halved; 3 disadvantage on attack rolls and saves; 4 maximum HP halved; 5 Speed zero; 6 death. Compute level-4 maximum as `max(1, floor(otherwise-applicable maximum HP / 2))`. Recompute from the otherwise-applicable maximum whenever it changes. Clamp current HP when the maximum falls; restoring the maximum does not heal. Flat Speed changes apply before halving; a zero-Speed condition overrides the calculation. A maximum-HP reduction alone is not damage and does not trigger a Wound save.

**NEW generic recovery:** At the end of a beneficial eight-hour long rest, remove one Exhaustion level from a living creature at levels 1–5 if it met the campaign's food/water requirements, the originating cause no longer actively imposes or refreshes Exhaustion, and no source-specific rule blocks removal of the chosen level. At most one generic level can be removed per 24 elapsed hours. Specific reviewed effects can remove additional levels as printed. A prerequisite such as Moisture Dependency's one-hour immersion unlocks recovery; it does not itself remove a level unless explicitly stated. Track blocked-source levels separately so another source's removable level may still be selected; the patient chooses a legal level to remove.

Exhaustion 6 causes death. Removing levels from the corpse never revives it. A resurrection effect must also leave the creature below 6 or it immediately dies again. Global Exhaustion, expedition Strain, Warrior serum Strain and Oracle's one-turn Revelation backlash remain separate records; this procedure clears none of those other tracks. See the [Strain namespace candidate](STRAIN_PLAYTEST.md) for its separately recorded review status.

## Dependence and Withdrawal

Preserve Core's existing substance procedures: resolve benefit and crash; a repeat dose before the next long rest requires the substance's dependence CON save; three uses within seven days cause tolerance that halves duration unless doubled; more than two doses before a long rest triggers the substance's severe complication and dependence advancement. This document supplies endpoints, not a replacement substance catalog. Use each item's reviewed dependence DC and severe complication. An item lacking its actual consequence remains in the item review queue rather than gaining an invented generic overdose result.

**Maintenance:** At each completed long rest, a new maintenance dose is due for each named dependence. Withdrawal applies immediately until a qualifying dose is taken after that rest; a dose taken before its completion cannot satisfy the new interval. The dose ends that substance's current symptoms until the next maintenance interval but does not remove dependence. Ordinary consumption time, stock, crash, tolerance and repeated-dose rules still apply. No free dose or Action is granted.

**Tolerance:** Record doses in a rolling seven-day window. After the third completed dose/use within that window, tolerance becomes active; subsequent uses have half duration unless doubled. The third ordinary use is not retroactively shortened. Count a doubled dose as two doses for tolerance, repeated-dose and overdose accounting; resolve its two-dose thresholds as one consumption event, with at most one dependence save for that event. Seven full days with no dose clears tolerance. One long rest does not clear tolerance. Track each substance separately.

**NEW dependence recovery project:** Complete seven consecutive project days without a dose of the named substance. Each day the patient spends one hour in treatment/recovery work and consumes one Supply. Choose Medicine, Religion or Alchemy at project start. At the end of the seventh full day, the designated practitioner (who may be the patient) makes that check against the substance's dependence DC, or NEW DC 14 if a direct Addicted effect supplied no substance DC. Success removes that named Addicted and its associated Withdrawal. Failure removes neither; a new attempt needs a new seven-day project. There is no extra automatic Wound on Critical Failure.

The existing Haven activity “Treat Dependence or Withdrawal” gives advantage on the next recovery check and prevents one ordinary withdrawal escalation after one full day under qualified care. For this bridge, a proficient practitioner spends an eight-hour care activity during a project day; that day's one-hour treatment requirement is included, not additional. Advantage applies once to the next recovery check and cannot be stockpiled. Different sources of advantage still do not stack. The activity does not independently cure dependence or erase a dose's printed crash.

Withdrawal imposes disadvantage on ability checks. “Disadvantage on RP recovery” affects an actual RP recovery roll only; deterministic Retune receives no invented arithmetic penalty. Oracle RC is not RP. The generic Withdrawal condition has no further severity track. An individual substance can add an explicitly reviewed duration or escalation; otherwise do not invent one. Symptom-removal magic does not remove dependence unless it explicitly does, but valid symptom suppression is compatible with completing a no-dose project.

## Intoxication

Use one dose-driven score from 0 to 5. Increase it only when an effect explicitly grants Intoxication. A direct effect saying “Intoxicated” supplies a minimum effective score of 2 for its printed duration, or NEW two hours when no duration is supplied. It does not add dose-driven points or count as a dose. Effective score is the greater of the dose-driven score and the active generic floor of 2. Generic timed floors of 3–5 do not exist. A source explicitly setting level 3–5 must individually define its dose-driven change or its own complete recovery exception before becoming operational. Each no-duration floor-2 application expires exactly two elapsed hours after application. Multiple direct floors do not stack, but the floor persists while any is active. Removing one leaves independent points and other direct applications intact.

| Score | Consequence |
|---|---|
| 0 | Sober; no Intoxication consequence. |
| 1 | Disadvantage on precise-memory checks. One available advantage use on a fear save. |
| 2 | Also disadvantage on precise DEX and INT checks. |
| 3 | Also Dazed and Speed −10 feet. |
| 4 | Also Unconscious for the level-4 timer and a poisoning save. |
| 5 | Also a medical emergency with a fixed one-hour deadline. |

The rows are cumulative. The Director identifies a “precise” check before rolling: fine manipulation or exact memory/analysis, not every possible use of DEX/INT. The player may spend the one fear-save advantage use before rolling. It refreshes only after effective score reaches 0 and a later new episode begins, never at each positive level. An explicit independent Dazed, Unconscious or Poisoned effect is not removed merely because intoxication ends.

**NEW natural reduction:** At dose-driven scores 1–3, one complete hour without new Intoxication removes one point; repeat each hour. A new positive gain resets that hourly timer even if a direct floor conceals the dose-driven change. A timed floor itself does not stop underlying points declining. At score 4 use its specific timer; score 5 cannot decay naturally. After a reduction to 3 or below, begin the next hourly interval at that transition. A timed floor can prevent the effective score from dropping until that application ends.

**NEW level 4:** On entering effective score 4 (or returning from treated 5), roll 1d4 once and set that many hours as the recovery deadline. Make a DC 14 CON save; on failure add Poisoned caused by intoxication while effective score is at least 4. Unconscious from this track lasts until that deadline unless cured earlier. Ending Unconscious alone does not clear points or reset the deadline. Reapplying score 4 without leaving it does not reroll or extend the deadline. At its deadline, if alive and no emergency is active, reduce dose-driven score to at most 3 and end track-caused Unconscious/Poisoned. A generic cure explicitly ending Intoxication removes all its track/floor records and track-caused consequences.

**NEW level 5:** On entering score 5, set a fixed emergency deadline one hour later and become/remain Unconscious. A jump directly from below 4 to 5 starts the emergency immediately; the level-4 recovery timer and poisoning save begin only after successful care returns it to 4. Additional gains at 5 never reset or extend it. A helper may spend ten uninterrupted minutes and one healer's-kit use, consumed at start, then make DC 15 WIS (Medicine). Success before the deadline ends the emergency, sets the dose-driven score to 4, adds one Wound if below three, and begins the level-4 timer/save. At three Wounds, successful emergency care prevents death without creating a fourth Wound; this is a specific provisional exception for this treatment. This direct Wound has no Injury roll and does not itself trigger a Wound save. Wound immunity prevents that added Wound where applicable.

Failure leaves the original emergency and deadline; another fully paid attempt is possible if it can finish before that deadline. At the exact deadline, death takes precedence over an unfinished or simultaneously finishing generic attempt. No natural score reduction can clear the emergency. A reviewed effect explicitly removing Intoxication or the emergency can end it by its own procedure. An immunity to Unconscious or Poisoned does not, by itself, prevent the separate emergency or death state.

## Corrupted

Use the condition's half healing, individually recorded Evil-source save disadvantage, aura and DC 15 WIS long-rest save. A failed long-rest save shifts the moral axis Good → Neutral → Evil without changing law/chaos. Never infer Evil from ancestry, species, faction, homeland or appearance. This label change does not compel beliefs, behavior, PvP, party separation or automatic oathbreaking. Specific conduct clauses still judge actual conduct.

**NEW generic cleansing:** One practitioner spends eight uninterrupted hours with one patient in a secure location, consumes one Supply at start, and makes INT (Religion) or INT (Arcana) against DC 15 at completion. Success removes Corrupted. Failure leaves it without any extra automatic Wound, condition or Exposure. No more than one generic attempt may complete for that patient in 24 elapsed hours; practitioners cannot stack concurrent attempts. The practitioner is working, while the patient may rest if otherwise eligible. If cleansing and the patient's long rest complete together, resolve cleansing first; make the Corrupted rest save only if it remains. A specific reviewed cleansing spell/item uses its own costs and procedure.

Guaranteed one-HP recovery from a natural-20 death save or the Stable recovery clock remains one HP: these are state-recovery rules, not healing effects. Ordinary one-point magical healing can still be halved to zero. It nevertheless ends generic Bleeding if it had positive pre-reduction healing potential.

## Unity Exposure — public provisional track

The source defines a 0–6 track with erosion of distinction and identity but no operational numeric threshold table was found in the bounded Core/V6/Director and current reference searches. GPT also reported no owner-approved numerical table in its available notebook history. The following is **NEW candidate mechanics**, not recovered setting truth. It grants no public knowledge of the exposure's hidden causes or identities.

Use the current row only; do not add lower-row modifiers.

| Score | Mechanical effect |
|---|---|
| 0 | No effect. |
| 1 | Tracked, without a generic numerical penalty. |
| 2 | −1 Perception/Investigation checks specifically distinguishing similar identities, copies, duplicates or conflicting sensory impressions. Declare this scope before rolling. |
| 3 | −1 INT and WIS ability checks. |
| 4 | −1 INT, WIS and CHA ability checks. |
| 5 | Disadvantage on INT, WIS and CHA ability checks. |
| 6 | Disadvantage on INT, WIS and CHA ability checks and saves. The character remains playable with player agency. |

Record changes only from explicit reviewed effects; cap at 0–6. These mechanics never decide a character's beliefs, loves, loyalty, factual memories, conduct or hidden revelations. A player can portray blurred memories or identity pressure without surrendering character control.

**NEW Anchor Project:** In a secure Haven or equivalent safe location, complete three full consecutive project days. Each day the patient spends two hours affirming chosen memories, relationships or personal distinctions and consumes one Supply. The player chooses the content. At the end of the third full day, make a WIS save against DC `10 + current Exposure`, including the track's actual penalties. Success reduces Exposure by one; failure does not. A new reduction requires a new full project. Ordinary rest does not reduce Exposure.

Any successful positive Exposure-gain event during the attempt interrupts it, including a gain capped at 6; prevented gains do not. Already consumed Supply remains spent. Only one Anchor Project per patient can be active. Specific reviewed removal effects may work differently. Director context and later source reconciliation remain separately packaged; private narrative information does not silently add numerical penalties or erase player agency.

## Names, dialects and modes

Record spoken comprehension, speaking, reading, writing and script familiarity separately. Knowledge and current ability to use it are different: deafness may stop you hearing a language you know; it does not remove that knowledge.

**NEW permanent-grant convention:** a permanent ordinary grant saying “know,” “one language,” or a background language row grants spoken comprehension, speaking, reading and writing in the language's attested ordinary written form, unless expressly narrowed. Temporary understanding, basic ideas, fragmentary writing and magical communication give only their specific modes or meaning.

Orc and Orcish are one identity; Mycelic and Sporetongue are one. **NEW chosen interpretation of the book's option:** Imperial's Westreach, Eastern Sigil and Northern Vale use Common mechanically, while retaining their cultural/register labels. They do not consume extra choices or decode ciphers. “Mycelian” is an ancestry/legacy label, not an alias for Mycelic.

Trollish and Giant remain distinct. Deep Cant, Deep Speech, Murkish, Forgotten Script, Runic and Resonant Cant remain distinct. Shared letters, an ancient description or a similar name does not establish mutual comprehension or permission to select an otherwise restricted language.

**NEW Primordial policy:** general Primordial and Auran, Aquan, Ignan and Terran are independently known, related competencies. Knowing one does not automatically grant any of the others. Elemental-Touched chooses general Primordial **or** the dialect matching its already selected affinity: air/Auran, water/Aquan, fire/Ignan, earth/Terran. This fills one grant. Its Aquan is the same language an Amphibian knows. Other sources granting Primordial give general Primordial unless they expressly offer a dialect choice.

Gnomish and Orcish use Dwarvish script. Knowing its letters does not teach either language's grammar, meaning or cultural context. Where no named script is given, record a language-local orthography without inventing a lore name. **NEW written-competency completion:** Runic grants its attested written content; Forgotten Script must identify the actual admitted written tradition. Unspecified spoken forms remain unspecified. Recognizing or copying characters alone does not understand them.

No grant creates anatomy, a pheromone emitter, hearing, sight, hands, writing implements or a magical channel. Mycelic's description does not supply an invented biological ability. An ordinary flat ink page is not tactile-readable merely because its reader knows the language; an actual touch-reading spell exception has its own scope.

The published names The Voice and Resonant Cant retain their existing restrictions; this chapter grants neither ordinary enrollment nor an automatic class entitlement. Their meanings and deeper relationships remain deferred. No hidden-language list is created here.

## Learn a language

**NEW ordinary course:** choose one language/dialect and the modes sought. Identify the learner, the relevant script, legitimate access, and an actual qualified instructor or a complete usable curriculum. An instructor needs the modes taught and a mutually usable channel. Self-study needs authentic explanations, examples, exercises and a way to check their meaning. An unknown inscription, an isolated translation, money or an Insight balance is not a curriculum. Spoken practice needs actual production and correction; comprehension-only magic does not supply it.

| Module | Active work |
|---|---:|
| Spoken comprehension and production | 240 hours |
| Literacy after knowing the language's semantics | 80 hours |
| Script/orthography portion included in that literacy | 40 hours |
| Script familiarity alone, without semantics | 40 hours |

A complete new spoken-and-written language requires **320 active hours**, or **280** with genuine prior knowledge of that same script. Literacy for a semantically known language takes 80 hours, or 40 with that script already known. A written-only language uses 240 hours of written semantics plus the 80-hour literacy module and grants only its attested written modes. Related dialects give no automatic discount. An explicit grant bypasses study only for the modes it actually grants; valid starting knowledge incurs no retroactive fee.

Credit complete **15-active-minute phases**. Interruption loses the unfinished phase's prospective credit; previous credit survives, while real time, materials and fees remain spent. A shorter final phase is allowed only to finish the exact module after a real source-specific adjustment. Missing instruction, access or a usable channel yields no progress. Log real losses separately. Administrative phases do not break actual concentration or evade Oracle Tongues' actual save and ten-minute loss.

**NEW tuition reference:** 1 gp per eight actual instruction hours, including ordinary lesson consumables the provider actually supplies. A real quote or voluntary teacher may differ. Self-study has no invented tutor fee but needs actual materials. Pay for actual instruction time, including time an interruption made unproductive. Round each actual final purchase once upward to copper; do not round every phase separately. Prepaid time and refunds follow the actual agreement. A price does not conjure a teacher, rare text, permission or equipment.

Use actual time within eight-hour Watches and the two-active-work-Watch ceiling, with governing rest, Strain and access limits. The tutor is occupied too. A minute cannot also fund guarding, travel, beneficial rest, crafting, research, another course, gaining Insight or spending Insight without an explicit rule allowing that concurrency. No calendar-day shortcut, INT/PB discount or pending feat applies.

Completion is deterministic after genuine required work and authentic final practice, included in the last required phase. There is no random final fluency roll, added examination period or completion fee. Record the acquired modes and their source. Gain no XP, PB, Expertise, formula, spell, rank, faction permission or another language. Partial study can establish particular recorded words; it does not satisfy a requirement to know the language.

**Example:** an Orcish-literate learner studies Gnomish with a qualified teacher and usable lessons. Shared Dwarvish script reduces the course to 280 hours, reference tuition 35 gp. A 40-minute lesson interrupted during its third phase gives 30 credited minutes but consumes 40 actual minutes; one invoice at the reference rate costs 9 cp. An applicable Tongues failure later removing ten credited minutes remains a real loss.

## Understand, translate or decipher

Plain accessible speech or text in a known language needs no comprehension roll. That does not establish its truth, solve a code, authenticate it, reveal technical context or recover missing facts. Remembering a specific message understood through temporary magic preserves that information after the effect ends; general competence does not persist.

| Task | Procedure | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Copy visible characters | Actual access, tools, stock and time | A facsimile; no certified meaning or magical encoding |
| **NEW** ordinary prose translation | Source reading and destination writing; ten active minutes per 250 words, proportionately rounded up to a minute, minimum one | Plain noncoded prose in the destination language; no roll merely for translation |
| **NEW** uncertain recognition | One minute; normally INT/History, DC 10 familiar attested style, 15 supported related form, 20 damaged but diagnostic evidence | Supported identity or relationship; no translation |
| **NEW** Translate/Decipher project | One preregistered supported passage of at most 250 words; eight active hours; declared evidence, method, output and DC | Only the supported passage or cipher layer |

Routine obvious recognition needs no roll. A nondiagnostic specimen cannot reveal its identity through a high roll. Translation speed does not replace formula-copying, magical encoding or contract-authentication procedures.

For the eight-hour project, register the actual source meaning or finite supported meaning, relevant parallel/grammatical/key evidence and missing sections before work. Linguistic reconstruction uses INT/History: DC 15 supported related dialect, 20 unfamiliar but adequately evidenced language, 25 damaged yet recoverable correspondence. A separate mundane cipher uses INT/Investigation: DC 15 adequate known key, 20 constrained ordinary analysis, 25 difficult but genuinely solvable damaged/incomplete key. A plainly usable key may remove uncertainty; it does not provide a missing underlying language.

Declare one lead and one applicable PB contribution. **NEW project-specific assistance:** one qualified assistant contributes +1 after all eight hours of actually useful participation. This does not add assistants to other procedures. Apply the existing Core task degrees and natural shifts.

Success supplies only the registered supported result. Critical Success grants no second passage, fluency, extra meaning, code bypass or banked labor. Failure leaves notes and spent work, without a certified translation. Critical Failure has the same informational result plus only a genuinely predeclared, independently lawful hazard. No failure fabricates authoritative lore. An inaccessible or unsupported meaning makes the project unqualified before work; a destroyed gap stays a gap.

A fresh attempt requires genuinely new evidence or a concretely different supported method, and fresh required work. Changing readers, dates, copies or formatting alone does not create evidence or reset an unchanged failed attempt. Information genuinely discovered can support later work; past hours and rewards are never credited twice.

Formula research and copying retain their trade gates, DC, minimum research time and one-hour/1-sp copying rule. Scribing Insight uses its separate procedure below. A subject-limited background information feature is not general translation. Pending research/language feats give no current discount or bonus.

## Communicate in a scene

**NEW finite bound:** each creature's aggregate free ordinary speech/signing must fit at most **six seconds per numbered round**. Warnings, replies and extra turns share that allowance. Outside initiative use actual conversational time. Brief communication costs no additional Action, but cannot activate a feature, move you, grant a Reaction or interrupt an already resolved event. A spell's words follow that spell's casting procedure, without a new universal word cap.

Longer deliberate exchanges take an Action for each additional six-second segment on a turn with that Action available. Off-turn lengthy delivery requires a real applicable permission, such as a legitimately readied communication Action, or waits. Surprise keeps its printed brief-communication permission without granting an unavailable Action. Respect voice, hands, consciousness and all other actual restrictions.

An interpreter must first perceive and understand the incoming message, then produce a form the recipient can perceive and understand. A short source phrase and rendition may fit an interval; a long statement or multiple relays cannot arrive instantaneously. Record when meaning reaches each recipient. Late interpretation cannot retroactively qualify a resolved check or effect. A translator lends no fluency, bonus or mental link.

**NEW party signals:** ten active minutes of mutual demonstration/rehearsal establishes up to six recorded simple cues for the actual participants, such as halt, approach, retreat, danger, left and right. A one-hand cue requires that usable hand and a receiver who sees it; a two-hand cue requires both. Light, distance, cover and attention must support actual perception. Six cues do not teach a fluent sign language, arbitrary sentences or codebreaking. A formal sign language needs an actual source/course.

Player accessibility is free of fictional action costs: explaining your character's intent at the table is not the character speaking, signing, providing V or violating an oath. You need not perform a voice or gesture to declare its fictional use.

**Example:** in a six-second interval a three-second Aquan warning followed by a three-second Common rendition can reach the second listener at the end. A response cannot precede that receipt. A thirty-second explanation through two interpreters cannot qualify an attack that has already resolved. A Deafened ally who sees a rehearsed retreat cue receives that cue, without satisfying a feature requiring the ally to hear a performance.

## Hearing, silence and magic

| Restriction or permission | Actual consequence |
|---|---|
| Deafened | Cannot hear; language knowledge, reading, signs and otherwise eligible mental channels remain. It does not by itself prevent own speech or V. |
| Silenced | Prevents V, command words, Chants and audible coordination. **NEW explicit completion:** includes deliberate ordinary spoken messages. It does not itself forbid thought, reading, writing, signs or a separately valid mental effect. |
| Silence the Caster combat action | Prevents verbal-component Reactions through its printed window, with its actual concentration check. It does not suppress ordinary speech or legal Action-time V casting. |
| V component | Requires that caster's actual audible speech. An interpreter, sign, telepathic phrase, playback, mimicry or another speaker cannot supply it. |

S, F, material, hand and access requirements remain separate. An explicit class exception waives only its stated requirements. Language knowledge grants no casting access, RP, repertoire or formula. Track overlapping prohibitions separately with their own sources and expirations: an operation stays blocked while any applicable prohibition remains. ## Select a spell

1. Choose the class through which you are learning/casting it. Check that class's school access and minimum **class** level on the card.
2. Use that class's spell rank and Core V2 cost. A different eligible class may receive the same spell at a different rank and level.
3. Record it in your allowed known, prepared or spellbook choices. An eligible catalog entry is not an automatic grant. Wizard and Druid keep their explicit preparation systems; fallback counts apply only where the class has no more specific rule.
4. Select only a spell marked `operational-playtest-draft` in this packet, or an operational spell expressly supplied by a class card. Other records stay visible in the unfinished queue.
5. A class card and an ordinary spell with the same name remain separate records with separate acquisition and costs. Knowing one does not grant the other. Oath spells, Matrix techniques and similar class spells use their own card.

Oracle uses RC and its Mystery/Curse system. Soldier and Warrior have no general Weave access. Dragoon first gains ordinary magic at class 3; Paladin at class 2. Sufficient RP, total character level, a class feature with the same name, or a borrowed spellbook cannot bypass a gate.

## Resolve a cast at the table

1. Verify the available Action/Bonus Action/Reaction, its exact trigger, components, targets, range and line of effect. No legal target means no activation or payment. A target in an area still needs the card's eligibility. Total cover blocks direct targeting unless expressly overridden.
2. Choose a spell from your actual repertoire. Determine its class-specific rank and RP cost: rank 0–9 costs **0/2/3/5/7/10/13/17/21/26**. Add explicitly printed extra costs; Resonance Shield adds 1 RP even when the caster receives it as a cantrip. Generic Overcast is excluded.
3. Read Dissonance **before** casting. Limit = max(4, 2 + PB + max(0, casting modifier)). At limit/limit+3/limit+6, ranked spells cost +1/+2/+3 RP. At limit+6 ordinary rank-1+ casting is blocked. Cantrips have no strain surcharge but still build Refrain. An expressly granted traumatic-casting exception pays the cost and its printed trauma; it grants neither rank nor repertoire access.
4. Commit the legal cast's RP, materials and other printed costs before any attack/save or interruption. Perform its components and establish concentration if required, ending incompatible prior concentration. An ordinary missed, saved-against or countered legal cast refunds nothing and never restores displaced concentration.
5. At this cast's beginning, apply ordinary Dissonance and Refrain once: 0 base for rank 0, 1 for ranks 1–5, 2 for ranks 6–9; consecutive same-named casts add Refrain +1/+2/+3, capped at +3. First cast or a different name adds +0. Apply the class's exact protected reduction, routing or vent and any hook whose printed trigger is beginning/casting. Weapon or idle turns do not reset the previous name/Refrain unless the class expressly says so. This chronological commitment occurs before the Counterspell window; a later Reaction cast updates its own history, and resuming the earlier cast does not update that history again.
6. Open legal cast-interruption Reactions, resolving nested counters last-in, first-out. A surviving cast then resolves its effect: spell attacks are d20 + PB + the actual casting ability modifier; save DC is 8 + PB + that modifier. Use the exact card's hit/failure/success results and ordinary damage/conditions. Outcome-dependent class hooks occur only at their printed timing and with the required actual result. No automatic cantrip scaling applies. A negated spell grants no success/hit/damage effect merely because its casting cost was paid.
7. Record concentration, exact expiration, per-rest use, summon and companion command obligations. A second spell cannot supply an ungranted Action, duplicate concentration or resource reset. A readied spell commits this casting sequence at preparation; release has no second cast, cost, cadence update or Counterspell window.

Countering requires an actual operational spell or class card, its repertoire/access and a legal remaining Reaction. The ordinary Counterspell is now reviewed; it is separate from the Mage and Wizard class cards. Dispel Minor, Dispel Resonance, Dispel Magic (Lesser) and Dispel Magic use their exact individual scopes. Rank-limited dispels inspect the original generating cast's spell rank, not RP cost or the dispeller's rank. Higher and unassigned source variants retain their own unfinished status.

The [exact notebook review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ABJURATION_RANK2_3_EXACT_REVIEW.md) confirms this authored timing interface and corrects the earlier binary-check proposal using the existing [Core roll rules](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md). Ordinary Counterspell uses its casting class's actual spellcasting ability + PB against **DC 10 + twice the triggering spell's actual rank**. | Natural d20 + modifier | DC | Existing task result | Counter result |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 20 + 0 | 22 | Failure improves to Success | Success |
| 1 + 9 | 10 | Success worsens to Failure | Failure |
| 1 + 20 | 10 | Critical Success worsens to Success | Success |

The target must be an actual pending spell with a recorded rank. The Director may use hidden source data without revealing the spell's identity/rank; attempting grants no free identification. Counterspell is itself a spell and can be countered. Negation refunds no costs and restores no prior concentration. Countering one spell is not whole-Action/turn hard denial and does not spend that combined ledger.

## Falling bridge — new provisional procedure

This is a newly authored table procedure agreed with the GPT notebook, **not recovered V6/Core V2 canon**. Focused searches of the current rulebook extract, Core V2 and mechanics/manual text found spell summaries but no operational falling clock or impact formula. Before promotion to canon, inspect the approved V6 environment/travel/hazard sections and archived environment tables. Preserve any older rule found and compare it explicitly.

When a creature loses support with no movement mode or effect keeping it aloft, it enters **Falling** immediately. Falling means unsupported; it grants no hovering, airborne walking or lateral movement. Track total distance descended during this fall and cumulative distance during its current uncontrolled portion, both initially zero.

**Timing:** If a fall begins during a regular initiative turn, set a fixed Fall Marker at the **end of that initiative slot in the following round**. Resolve the first Falling Step there, then one at the same marker each round. Reactions and extra turns use the enclosing regular initiative slot; an event between slots uses the most recently completed slot. Extra turns, extra Actions and initiative changes neither move nor multiply the marker. This gives every participant one normal turn opportunity before the first descent; inability to act still matters and no free rescue action is granted. A caster still needs legal targets within range when spending their Action.

Outside initiative, when timing matters, establish an order before descent and use a virtual slot immediately before its first regular slot as the initiating slot. The first step occurs when that virtual slot next recurs, after everyone has had one normal turn opportunity. When no rescue or other timing decision is possible, the Director can resolve the same descent and impact calculation directly. This is an explicit timing abstraction, not a model of physical acceleration.

If a fall begins after initiative has been established but before any regular initiative slot has yet completed, treat the virtual pre-round slot as the most recently completed slot for Fall Marker purposes.

**Ordinary descent:** At each step descend up to **300 feet**, stopping on a supporting surface. Add the distance to both trackers. On landing while uncontrolled, take **min(10, floor(uncontrolled distance / 20))d6 bludgeoning damage**. The uncontrolled distance includes earlier steps; never use only the final step's remainder.

**Feather Fall:** The spell retains its **Action** casting time and reduces descent to at most **60 feet per step**. When it takes effect, set uncontrolled distance to zero: the magic dissipates prior uncontrolled momentum in this abstraction. Keep total fall distance. If landing while it remains active, damage is **min(3, floor(total fall distance / 20))d6 bludgeoning**. This explicitly limits impact exposure without guaranteeing a harmless landing. When the spell ends aloft, reset uncontrolled distance to zero, then accumulate ordinary descent from that point at the existing marker; expiry grants no immediate extra step. Its one-minute maximum ends immediately before the caster's regular turn ten rounds after casting. If expiry and a step coincide, resolve expiry first. Earlier landing or cessation of Falling ends the spell on that target as printed.

Apply damage defenses only when their actual wording covers that damage. After damage, Falling ends; a creature suffering any positive falling damage lands **Prone** unless an explicit feature prevents it. Less than 20 relevant feet produces zero damage. Forced movement that removes support starts a fall but adds no separate fall damage. Regaining genuine support, secure support from a hold, or flight ends Falling without resolving an uncompleted impact; teleporting safely onto support likewise ends it. A later loss of support begins a new fall with new trackers and marker. Completed impact and damage cannot be undone by later casting.

| Scenario | Steps to land | Impact |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ordinary 10 feet | 1 | 0 |
| Ordinary 20 feet | 1 | 1d6 |
| Ordinary 300 feet | 1 | 10d6 |
| Ordinary 310 feet | 2 | 10d6 |
| Ordinary 610 feet | 3 | 10d6 |
| Feather Fall active through a 310-foot fall | 6 | 3d6 |
| 120 feet slowed, spell ends aloft, then 190 feet uncontrolled | 3 | 9d6 |

The 300-foot ordinary step, impact formulas, momentum reset, marker and duration conventions are provisional inventions. The source supplies Feather Fall's Action, five targets and 60-foot slowed descent. Wider hazards, equipment catches, flight loss and environmental damage still need the combat/campaign pass.

# Creature companions: life, commands and identity

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED: 121 targeted checks and 2,800 Ranger conversion states.** This overlay discusses 100 exact passages from Druid, Mage, Mirrorsage, Ranger and Wizard, supported by five frozen common paragraphs. It closes no full class, form, temporary-HP system or complete runtime by itself. [Source register](CREATURE_LIFECYCLE_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md), [source integrity](CREATURE_LIFECYCLE_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json), [behavior checks](CREATURE_LIFECYCLE_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json).

The original class cards and frozen class guide remain intact. The notebook's first classification, boundary reconciliation and event-model decisions are preserved in the audit folder. Where the historical first reply differs from the later boundary replies, the later explicit resolution controls. In particular, Auto-Raise is automatic, its new minion cannot act at all in the creation round, and Mirrorsage Charm was not in the older 219-source control closure.

## At the table

Keep one companion command and one offensive companion allowance per owner per numbered round, including multiclass companions and devices. A normal command costs your Bonus Action. A damaging companion action, or Mage/Wizard control action, spends the offensive allowance. A pure support command spends only the command. The earlier device ledger's internal field named `damage` now represents this shared offensive allowance; its public behavior remains compatible with existing device checks.

Issue ordinary commands during your regular turn. The selected companion moves and performs its command immediately after your whole turn, in an attached phase. It receives no extra independent turn. If it or its target becomes ineligible before execution, the command fails without refund. Your later incapacity or removal alone does not cancel an issued command; actual concentration/source ending can. Uncommanded companions can move defensively and Dodge, subject to their conditions; this grants no generic Reaction or autonomous attack/control.

Use the owner's original regular companion markers for recharge and previous/next-turn references. Extra turns, initiative changes and removal do not restart those markers. The attached phase's event-resolution checkpoint is distinct: it refreshes no Reaction, recharge, Action, death save or regular duration clock.

# Reputation — Canon Interaction Rules

**Status:** Playable canon

Reputation records how Aethel's institutions respond to the character. It is not a morality score and it is not a hidden multiplier on the laws of magic.

## Scale

Faction standing is stored as `{ [factionId]: score }` on the character save, normally from **−3 (Hated)** through **+3 (Honored)**. Backgrounds and play can set or change starting standing.

## What reputation can change

A faction may change:

- prices, credit, insurance, salvage rights, and expedition sponsorship;
- access to restricted libraries, teachers, rituals, recipes, laboratories, temples, circles, and sanctuaries;
- information quality, contacts, safe houses, legal treatment, hostility, and political support;
- availability of a **named** focus, training feature, consumable, or scene benefit whose rules are written explicitly.

## What reputation does not change automatically

Reputation does **not** silently modify:

- a spell's Resonance Rank;
- base RP cost;
- natural maximum RP;
- Dissonance gained from a cast;
- the Frayed / Discordant / Fractured thresholds;
- a character's moral alignment.

If a guild teaches a cheaper technique or a shrine grants a recovery boon, that is an explicit earned benefit, not proof that the Weave itself favors members of that institution.

## Magic connection

The universal magic rules are in [`RESONANCE_CANON.md`](./RESONANCE_CANON.md). Faction standing can provide **tools for dealing with magic**, but never rewrites the underlying resonance law merely because the character is liked or hated.

## Companion implementation

- `src/data/reputation.js` owns faction definitions and starting standing.
- `character-storage.js` persists the reputation map.
- `resonance-economy.js` retains compatibility helper names for old saves/code, but automatic reputation-to-RP and reputation-to-spell-cost modifiers return **0** under current canon.

This separation is deliberate: institutions matter socially and materially; Resonance/Dissonance remain metaphysical rules.

# Shared rules for the class playtest drafts

**Provisional design integration, 8 October 2026.** These rules make the class drafts usable together for testing. They preserve each protected class engine while specifying missing timing and replacing conflicting old percentages. They do not rewrite the approved Word books. Original descriptions and alternate registry entries remain in `data/playtest/class_sources`.

## Reading a class card

Use the class's own level, never total character level, for gates and effects. **L** means that class level; **S** is 1/2/3/4 at class levels 1/5/11/17. **M** means max(1, the class ability modifier), for effect a mounts only. Attacks use d20 + normal character proficiency + the actual appropriate ability modifier. Class save DC is 8 + normal proficiency + actual class ability modifier. Negative modifiers still apply to attacks and DCs. One tile is 5 ft. Fractions round down unless specified. Distances cannot be negative.

A weapon attack uses its usual ability, weapon die and damage type. A technique that says “make one weapon attack” replaces your Action with that attack; it does not also grant a normal Attack Action or Extra Attack. Generic attack-speed language has no effect beyond the exact attacks printed in the draft. A spell attack uses the class's stated casting ability. Natural 1 misses and natural 20 hits/critically doubles damage dice; flat bonuses do not double. A save succeeds at DC; “fails by 10” means the total is at least 10 below DC. Critical-range improvements never stack; use the broadest one.

An ability is known only if granted or selected by the draft schedule. Satisfy all printed prerequisites, target legality, action availability, recharge and resource costs before spending anything. A failed legal attack/save attempt still pays; an illegal activation spends nothing. No resource goes below 0 or above its cap. A class feature name shared with a spell does not grant both versions; use the version selected, with its own cost and timing. Names and source text are preserved; the current card is the operational draft.

## Action and timing limits

One regular Action, one Bonus Action if a feature permits it, normal movement and one Reaction between starts of your turns. A free trigger costs no Action only if expressly stated. All grants share **one extra full Action per creature per round**. An extra Action cannot grant another Action, recharge itself, or start another extra-Action grant. It supplies no extra Bonus Action or Reaction. A card granting additional attacks is not permission to repeat all class riders on every hit: obey each rider's frequency.

Recharge N sets a counter to N after use; reduce once at the start of the owner's regular initiative turn, whether able to act or not. Extra turns/Actions do not tick it. Outside combat tick once per 6 elapsed seconds, without double counting. Recharge 2 used on turn 1 is ready on turn 3. A positive counter can be reset/shortened at most once per ability per round. Zero counters are not legal reset targets and expend no reset use. Resets never restore RP or per-rest uses or grant an immediate activation.

An encounter is a genuine scene of uncertain opposition chosen by the Director, not a player declaration used to reset resources. No encounter gain from attacking allies, one's summons, harmless animals, helpless captives or reused corpses. Out-of-combat abilities retain all printed costs and time. Short-rest means a completed uninterrupted hour of permitted recovery; long-rest means a completed 8-hour Rest Watch. This time convention is a draft integration. Expedition pressure, supplies, safe locations and rest debt still matter. A long rest also refreshes short-rest uses; a short rest never refreshes long-rest uses. Weekly uses refresh after seven full in-world days, not repeated rests.

## Targets, concentration and control

Unless expressly stated, perceive the target, remain within range and have line of effect; total cover blocks targeting. “Ally” includes self unless it says OTHER. A list cannot contain a creature twice. Select up to the printed limit; an empty target list is not a valid way to farm activation benefits. Zones remain at their chosen point unless described as an aura; allies can leave and lose their benefits. An aura requires its owner conscious unless the card supplies a bounded exception. An effect ending at “end next turn” means the affected creature's next turn only when the card says target's; otherwise the user's.

One concentration slot for all spells, Chants, Veinweaves, forms or zones that require concentration. Starting another ends the old before the new effect resolves, except for an explicit limited linked-effect rule. Damage prompts CON save against max(10, floor(damage/2)); incapacitation or a failed save ends concentration. The round-down convention is a deliberate pilot interpretation. Concentration does not demand a Bonus Action unless maintenance says so. For a paid 3-pulse effect, start is pulse 1; pay maintenance on each of the next 2 regular turns by turn end for pulses 2/3. Missing payment ends it at that turn's end; otherwise it ends at start of turn 4. No repeated start triggers on maintenance.

Forced movement does not provoke opportunity attacks unless explicitly stated, cannot place a creature inside solid matter, and stops at an obstacle. Grapples use the card's save/DC, can be escaped with an Action and STR(Athletics) or DEX(Acrobatics) against that DC, and end beyond reach. A root sets Speed 0 but does not remove Actions. Slows reduce Speed to minimum 0. Silence blocks verbal spells/audible abilities, not all thought or all class features. Charmed effects never determine a player's beliefs; use only the printed action restrictions.

No repeated hard denial without a new save and cost. For this class suite, a creature can suffer **Stunned, compelled loss of its whole Action/turn, or equivalent hard denial from a given character at most once per encounter**, across that character's class features; later such riders fail while damage and soft riders resolve normally. Record source and target. This draft guard is broader than the older Oracle-only ceiling and is an explicit balance proposal. Reaction denial, Speed reduction, penalties and Frightened do not count as whole-turn loss. Do not silently waive boss immunities, legendary defenses or anatomy.

## Damage, healing, stacking and companions

Roll once for each shared area/pulse and apply saves/defenses to each target separately; separate attacks roll separately. Halve once for a successful save and apply resistance/immunity normally. Same-named conditions/bonuses do not stack unless a printed cap allows it; same-stat flat bonuses from these class techniques use the strongest. Different resources remain separate. Damage reduction from these class features uses the strongest flat reduction, then applies resistance; it cannot create negative damage or healing. Temporary HP never stack; choose the larger remaining amount. Immunity is not reduced resistance.

Repeated permanent HP recovery must consume finite RP, a per-rest use or another finite resource; a combat-generated gauge alone never enables unlimited healing. Healing cannot exceed maximum HP or erase Wounds, death consequences, debt or Corruption unless explicit. Downed is living at 0 HP; dead is different. Resurrection requires a willing soul and sufficiently intact body, obeys its time window, cannot create a duplicate and never refunds the feature on failure to meet known prerequisites. Sacrificial HP is actual unpreventable loss, cannot be redirected or paid with temporary HP, and is not damage for resource triggers. It cannot reduce the donor below 1 unless a card expressly grants a death-triggered effect.

No damage/healing copy repeats the source's costs, procs, resource generation, critical bonus dice, buffs, actions, cooldown resets or duration. Compute fractions once, capped at 100% of one stored source unless an explicit card states a separately priced higher amount. Copies still cause ordinary damage consequences, concentration checks and death. A copy cannot copy another copy. A target/source record must refer to an actual resolved event, not merely a known ability name.

Where a class card calls for a **standard companion** without a more specific profile, use: Small or Medium; AC 12+floor(PB/2); HP 2 L; walking Speed 30 ft; saves equal owner's PB; one melee or ranged attack (reach 5 ft/range 30 ft) at owner's class attack bonus, damage S d6 of the printed type. It has no independent class features, resources, loot, death triggers or extra turns. All companions belonging to one character share one Bonus Action command and **one damaging attack/action total per round** unless a specifically priced feature grants more. Without a command they move and Dodge. Act immediately after owner. A standard companion lasts 1 minute, disappears at 0 HP and cannot be healed for free by dismissing/resummoning. The creation cost must be paid again. Creature-specific stat blocks override this profile only where explicitly printed.

## Ordinary spells: one explicit test configuration

Use the manifest-owned **Core Systems Known Descent V 2** class RP tables and rank costs: rank 0–9 costs 0/2/3/5/7/10/13/17/21/26; Grand 32. Follow `src/data/class-spell-progression.js` for each class's rank gates and the existing spell catalog for class/school access. Having enough RP never bypasses a rank gate. Oracle has Revelation Charges, and Soldier/Warrior have no general RP spellcasting. Multiclass spell access is determined separately per class; do not add complete class pools or use total level to unlock a rank. This suite's printed pool tables are single-class; use the existing multiclass pool formula with the new constituent Core V 2 pools for mixed characters.

Four classes have no direct Core V 2 pool row. For this pilot, Crimson Agent uses the Cleric curve multiplied by 0.5; Dragoon, Monk and Thief use that curve multiplied by 0.35, rounded to nearest integer with halves upward, minimum 1. These fallback factors come from the preserved `src/data/resonance-economy.js`; they are explicitly distinguished from direct book tables. The generic Core V 2 Oracle RP row is rejected for this class suite because Oracle's protected class contract uses Revelation Charges only. Oracle never receives RP or ordinary spell access. Retune here means one recovery at the end of a completed short rest, not an unrestricted action.

For a reproducible pilot, retain the protected **Dissonance** layer with Core V 2 numeric RP costs. This combination is a new integration decision: do not also roll a second historical Burn/fizzle system on top of it. Limit=max(4, 2+PB+max(0, casting modifier)). Before a ranked cast, Dissonance at limit/limit+3/limit+6 adds 1/2/3 RP respectively; at limit+6 ordinary casters cannot cast rank 1+. At limit+3 ordinary Overcast is unavailable. A cast then adds base Dissonance 0 at rank 0, 1 at ranks 1–5, 2 at ranks 6–9. Immediate repeated casts of the same named spell add 1, 2, then 3 maximum. Another named spell resets the repeat counter but not accumulated strain. Apply the class's exact cadence reduction/vent; never infer a free RP reduction. Printed class techniques pay printed costs and cause no automatic spell Dissonance unless tagged or expressly described as spells, Echo releases or Matrix casts. For a Mage/Wizard class card tagged as a spell, use the rank printed in normalized data; its rank is fixed at acquisition and does not rise with S. Other techniques are not counterspell able unless their card says so.

Retune recovers max(0, round(max RP/4)+casting modifier), never above maximum, and clears Dissonance. A long rest restores RP and clears Dissonance. Optional 10-minute meditation once/day recovers positive casting modifier RP and reduces Dissonance by PB+positive modifier. A regular turn with no spell or magical class ability loses 1 Dissonance; an Action spent Grounding without casting loses PB instead (not both). Merely ending an encounter does not clear accumulated Dissonance. Refrain survives idle/weapon turns unless a class explicitly clears it. Lich/Necromancer may force ranked casts through Fracture; after resolution take direct unpreventable trauma equal to rank×1/2/3 at the three strained states, minimum 1, based on state before casting. This trauma cannot generate resources or trigger damage-sharing. They still pay RP and meet rank gates.

Generic Overcast is excluded from the initial suite configuration until its options are separately fixed; cards such as Overchannel have their own exact costs and gates. Core V 2's original Burn procedures, older rank×2 costs and smaller companion RP tables remain preserved as alternatives, not silently combined. This configuration is suit able for comparing class drafts, not a claim that all historical magic sources already agree.

## Spell repertoires and acquisition

Preserve explicit class spellbook/preparation rules where given. For classes missing a known-spell count, this suite proposes: full casters know 3 cantrips at 1, 4 at 4, 5 at 10 and choose 2 ranked spells at first spell access plus 1 each later class level; hybrid/half/minor casters know 2 cantrips at first cantrip access and 3 at class 10, and choose 2 ranked spells at first ranked access plus 1 on each later even class level. At a long rest, a known caster may replace one known spell with a legal same-or-lower rank selection. This fills an actual missing rule and does not replace a more specific Druid prepared list or Wizard spellbook. Bonus spells expressly granted by a class are additional. No unnamed or mechanically unfinished catalog spell becomes complete merely by entering this repertoire; select operational spells for the test and record them.

Scheduled selection applies only where the class document says so. At each milestone choose distinct eligible entries; no banked Skill Points. Automatic engines, ASIs, feats, forms and finales do not also consume a choice unless stated. Ordinary-class schedule:4 Base at 1 (at least 2 active), 2 Base at 2; 2 Arch at 3 (at least 1 active); alternating 1 Base/Arch at 4/6/8/11/13/15/17/19 and 1 Arch at 5/7/9; choose Hero at 10 and 2 Hero (at least 1 active), then 1 Hero at 12/14/16/18; finale 20. If a class has no source Arch capstone, level 9 has the printed class-specific grant or another choice, explicitly shown. The individual schedule and prerequisite checks win over this summary. ASI or eligible feat at 4/8/12/16/19, separate from choices, except Oracle uses its explicit 4/8/14/19 schedule. Druid, Oracle and Paladin use their own schedules.

## Source and review status

The owner asked to extend the Bard treatment to all classes. Each draft separates the original wording, provisional numerical specification, acquisition and examples. Earlier contradictory level-table entries are retained as source evidence and marked reconciled/replaced for this draft; never stack them on top of the new schedule. Automated checks cover acquisition, source completeness and selected resource invariants. Human table play is still needed to judge balance, fun, and numerical tuning.


## Core condition reference

The following descriptions are preserved from [Core Systems Known Descent V2](../../data/public/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Data_v2_Known_Descent.json). The class suite adds its explicit duration, escape and hard-denial limits; it does not give the same named condition a different meaning in each class. Dread, Grief, Bleed and other custom riders use their card’s exact definition.

| Condition | Core V2 rule |
|---|---|
| Blinded | Cannot see; automatically fails sight checks; attacks have disadvantage and attacks against it have advantage. |
| Charmed | Cannot willingly harm the charmer; charmer has advantage on social checks against it. |
| Deafened | Cannot hear and fails hearing checks; verbal coordination may fail. |
| Frightened | Disadvantage while source is visible and cannot willingly move closer. |
| Grappled | Speed 0; ends if grappler is incapacitated or reach is broken. |
| Incapacitated | Cannot take actions or reactions. |
| Invisible | Cannot be seen normally; attacks against it have disadvantage and its attacks have advantage until location is revealed. |
| Paralyzed | Incapacitated, cannot move or speak, fails Strength/Dexterity saves, adjacent hits are critical. |
| Poisoned | Disadvantage on attacks and ability checks. |
| Prone | Crawl or stand; melee attackers within 5 ft. have advantage; ranged attackers have disadvantage. |
| Restrained | Speed 0; attacks against have advantage, own attacks and Dexterity saves have disadvantage. |
| Silenced | Cannot use verbal components, command words, Chants, or audible coordination. |
| Staggered | Cannot react, loses Guard, and the next forced movement gains +5 ft. Ends at start of next turn. |
| Stunned | Incapacitated, cannot move, fails Strength/Dexterity saves, attacks against have advantage. |
| Unconscious | Incapacitated, unaware, drops held items, falls Prone, adjacent hits are critical. |

# Crafting, harvesting and preservation

**Status: REVIEWED authored operational PLAYTEST crafting/harvesting/preservation framework.** This supplement makes the shared procedure executable. It does not approve any of the 687 recipe effects, infer missing magic-item powers, approve balance, or change the companion runtime. An unreviewed recipe may be executed only as an isolated framework test of access, scheduling, ingredients, crafting check, quality, yield, trade XP, preservation or price-reference behavior. Its unfinished output effect grants no gameplay benefit, activation, statistic, condition, spell-like effect, charge, duration, resource change or market classification beyond fields already independently reviewed. Normal campaign use of the finished product requires that recipe's output/effect card to be separately completed and reviewed.

The mechanical source is Crafting Bible V4 (687 recipes, 696 material records, 16 trades); the public V5 book contains 433 formulas and 604 materials. Preserve all source IDs and visibility: 433 public, 39 restricted, 215 Director-only recipes. Public availability does not mean free ownership of a formula. Public dossiers must not expose the other 254 recipes or 92 restricted materials. Cosmology remains outside this review until after the authorized GitHub push is verified.

The [actual GPT review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CRAFTING_ENGINE_EXACT_REVIEW.md) conditionally approved this framework; all eight required repairs are applied. Exact source text, hashes and paragraph/line bindings are in `docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/CRAFTING_ENGINE_SOURCE_EVIDENCE.json` at the game root. In this supplement, **Source** identifies recovered procedure; **Completion** identifies a new bounded interpretation. The original JSON, books and historical procedures remain unchanged.

## One work order, one batch

Before work, record the recipe ID and visibility, crafter and trade level, actual formula access, batch quantity, chosen ability, tools and station, component lots and substitutions, assistants, DC, expected active hours, work schedule, final product profile and market quotation. Record whether a product is an ordinary item, a magical item, a consumable or an alteration to an existing item. The name alone cannot decide that classification.

Check eligibility and reserve actual ingredients before beginning. Perform the required active work. Make one completion check for the entire batch; resolve quality, catalyst retention and failure recovery once. Debit consumed components, record returned components, add only actual finished units, and record trade XP. An interrupted batch is the same work order, with the same reserved ingredients. Neither interruptions nor moving to a new station create another roll, yield or first-craft award.

**Source:** quantity, difficulty, components, workRequirements and craftingCheck come from the exact recipe. **Completion:** recipe quantity is the number of finished units in one batch. Component quantities and costs are for that batch, not for each finished unit. Do not multiply components or recommended batch value by output quantity a second time. This interpretation applies to the new playtest projection; the ambiguous source `resultItem.value` is retained unchanged.

An unfinished output profile is a real dependency. The framework cannot invent a spell effect, charge recharge, activation action, target, range, save, duration, stacking rule, output weight or item price merely because a recipe has a `developed` label.

## Training and recipe access

**Source:** a character lacking the trade or the required tool proficiency has disadvantage and cannot attempt formulas above recipe skill level 4. Formulas above level 4 normally require a formula, schema, pattern or documented oral tradition. All 687 source formula flags agree with this threshold. Trade levels run from 1 to 20, separately from character level, class stage, PB, spell rank and material tier.

**Completion:** the primary-tool bindings in `CRAFTING_TRADE_REFERENCE.md` define the relevant training. A character who already has the listed proficiency may initialize that trade at level 1, with zero trade XP, without an extra proficiency grant. Merely owning the kit grants neither PB nor a trade level. Trade training and primary-tool proficiency acquired through this procedure are one credential, not two PB contributions. Existing explicit trade-level grants remain intact. Being proficient with unrelated tools, Arcana or Survival does not automatically give this credential.

An untrained crafter has effective trade level 0. Recipes of skill levels 1–4 can be attempted with the source disadvantage when otherwise physically possible. A trained crafter can attempt recipes up to `max(4, current trade level)`. Above level 4 the crafter must also possess or be given legitimate access to the exact formula. A trained level-1 novice does not lose the basic recipes available to an untrained character. Missing necessary physical tools or the station prevents the attempt; disadvantage does not manufacture either.

For a new credential during play, complete 80 active training hours with a willing instructor proficient in that primary tool and at least level 5 in that trade. Pay a default 10 gp tuition for the course, plus actual tool ownership or rental and living costs. Hours cannot overlap other work or rest. Completion grants that tool proficiency and trade level 1 with zero XP, once; repeated courses give no duplicate benefit. This is a new playtest training route, not a revision of class/ancestry/background grants. A named source's specific training route wins for its own grant.

Source rank bands (Novice, Apprentice, Journeyman, Expert, Master, Grandmaster) are descriptions of the catalog, not another hard tier gate. Forty-nine records sit outside the printed rank/tier bands. Use their exact skillLevel and explicit prerequisites rather than silently changing those recipes or denying them by a second band test. Public Tier I–V remains the public knowledge ceiling regardless of a character's high trade level. Restricted and Director recipes require actual in-world access and their separately reviewed cards; a rank title cannot reveal them.

## The crafting check

**Source:** `d20 + chosen ability modifier + proficiency contribution + tool bonus + facility bonus + assistant bonus`, against the recipe difficulty. Choose one of the recipe's printed ability options before rolling. **Completion:** do not add the numerical trade level to the check. PB comes from total character level, once, when qualified by actual primary-tool training; an explicit applicable expertise feature replaces that contribution with its stated multiplier. Training in both a skill and the tool cannot double it.

Ordinary functional tools and a suitable ordinary facility each give a bonus of +0. They permit the work. A specific reviewed item, facility or feature may give a stated bonus; similar descriptive words such as fine, superior or research station do not invent a crafting bonus. The expedition research station's +2 research/identification applies to those checks, not crafting. Same-named bonuses do not stack. At trade level 10, choose and record one specialty; its source +1 applies only to a work order within that specialty. No automatic free ingredient substitution follows from the word specialty.

Each qualified assistant gives +1, up to the recipe's `maximumAssistants` (0–3). They must possess the relevant primary-tool proficiency, be eligible to attempt that recipe, and work all of its required active hours alongside the lead. Formula access can be shared for this work order. Assistance does not reduce time, waive ingredients, award extra output or grant assistant trade XP. Assistants cannot assist multiple simultaneous orders or perform a separate Watch activity during those same hours. General team assistance cannot bypass a recipe's zero-assistant limit.

In a safe suitable workshop, a trained lead may use 10 on the die if the recipe is at least five skill levels below their current trade level. This replaces the die, is not a natural 10/20/1, and uses the same bonuses, costs and hours. It is unavailable when under threat or when actual disadvantage remains on the crafting check. Declare it before rolling; a failed roll cannot be replaced afterward.

## Active time and expedition scheduling

**Source recovered from public V5 P11–12 and P88:** an Opening is 100 days, or 2,400 elapsed hours. The V4 system's 240-hour references are stale. Crafting hours represent active work, not free downtime. The recipe records consistently convert a workday to 8 active hours, a workweek to 40, and a workmonth to 160. These are work units, not a promise that every calendar week/month has that many days.

**Completion:** use `activeWorkHours` when present. Five Director-only one-year recipes have null hours; for this framework only, one workyear is 12 workmonths = 1,920 active hours. Preserve their source null and mark the overlay as new; these formulas remain individually unreviewed. A time-mode name is a station/access requirement, not permission to reduce required hours. An eight-hour recipe labeled expedition still needs all eight hours.

Field work requires its actual portable tools and a suitable place. A recipe is field-capable only when its `fieldCraftable` flag permits it; the fact that its trade is generally field-capable is insufficient. Expedition-mode work needs a fortified camp or research station. Workshop work needs a proper workshop. Haven-mode work needs a named secure workshop and storage. Legacy/special work needs a protected long-term facility or an explicitly supported between-season arrangement. Shorter time from a feature does not erase the recipe's station/access requirement.

Schedule one eight-hour Watch at a time. A member assigned to crafting, gathering or preservation can perform compatible sequential tasks within that Watch, recording actual minutes. The unused minutes are not another full team activity. Travel, guarding, assisting, spellcasting, training and work cannot all claim the same minutes; only an explicit ability can authorize concurrent tasks. Each character may schedule at most two active Watches and must satisfy the separately reviewed rest rules; this is a ceiling, not an exemption from fatigue, interruption or danger. For this supplement, an active work Watch means time committed to crafting, harvesting, preservation, trade training, formula research or assisting those activities. The two-Watch ceiling limits this framework's work contribution; it does not by itself resolve whether another reviewed subsystem permits a distinct noncrafting activity in the remaining Watch. Rest, Strain, fatigue and expedition legality continue to come from their own governing rules. An eight-hour beneficial Long Rest cannot simultaneously be eight hours of crafting. Trance's sleep reduction does not shorten the required Long Rest or grant free working time.

Workday notation is normalized to active hours before a valid speed feature applies. Forge Dwarf Master Craftsman reduces eligible artisan-tool creation hours by 25%; use hours × 0.75, rounding upward only to the next whole minute. It does not shorten rest, travel, ingredient growth/spoilage, training, another person's work, harvesting, or a separately fixed natural-remedy/tinker racial procedure. It does not shorten a recipe's independently stated incubation or calendar wait. Other applicable time modifiers require their own actual text; no unprinted stacking multiplier is created here.

Long orders may be paused between active phases. A default phase is at most eight active hours. Completing a phase safely permits secure storage and later resumption without lost progress. Forced interruption inside a phase loses only unfinished progress in that phase; completed phases remain. No crafting roll occurs yet. Reserved perishables still age, and explicit physical destruction can lose actual inventory. There is no arbitrary full restart or repeated free quality roll. Before an uninterrupted-phase order begins, record its phase lengths and storage needs; absent a more specific formula, use this default.

At the season boundary, unfinished work continues only if its actual location, workers and storage remain legally and physically available under the existing campaign rules. The 2,400-hour Opening does not grant 2,400 labor hours per character. The Haven activity 'Brew a Batch' supplies a workday assignment (8 hours), not automatic completion of every recipe regardless of its own duration.

## Quality and finite output

These are **crafting outcome labels**, separate from equipment grade and Core artifact market condition. An Exceptional craft does not automatically become Exceptional equipment (+3 statistics), and a Masterwork craft does not create a new grade or a magic item. An item named Superior does not obtain equipment-grade bonuses unless its reviewed profile explicitly binds that grade.

Resolve this specific six-band crafting table instead of general expedition outcome shifts. A natural 1 is a Mishap even if the total is high. A natural 20 uses its numerical total with no extra band shift. A margin of −10 or lower is a Mishap.

| Total minus DC | Result | Procedure |
|---|---|---|
| 10 or more | Masterwork | Choose 150% batch yield, rounded down, or the improvement option below; also preserve one eligible catalyst unit. |
| 5 through 9 | Exceptional | Choose 125% batch yield, rounded down, or the improvement option below. |
| 0 through 4 | Standard | Listed number of ordinary finished units. |
| −1 through −4 | Flawed | If base batch quantity is at least 2, produce half quantity rounded down, with ordinary unit effects. If quantity is 1, make one item with a defined flaw below. |
| −5 through −9 | Failed | No product; recover 25% of consumed non-catalyst input quantity for each material identity, rounded down to that material's permitted unit. |
| −10 or less, or natural 1 | Mishap | No product; lose consumed inputs, return nonconsumed tools, and roll the mishap procedure. |

**Completion:** quality choices are declared after the check, once for the whole batch. Extra yield does not itself consume another batch of ingredients; it represents reduced processing waste. For physical outputs the card must specify lawful packaging and output mass; total output cannot exceed actual retained material plus explicitly supplied extra mundane carrier/packaging. A yield increase cannot create missing bottles, duplicate a unique named core, or duplicate the existing item being enchanted. Such an order uses its legal improvement option or retains Standard quantity and its quality label. Floor arithmetic may give no extra units; no fractional item or banked remainder is created.

The default improvement option increases explicitly defined maximum structural item HP by 25% (Exceptional) or 50% (Masterwork), rounded down, minimum +1. Current HP increases by the same amount for the new undamaged item. It never increases creature HP, AC, damage, save DC, spell rank, RP, charges or capacity. A recipe card may replace this with one precise property/charge option reviewed for that recipe. With neither known structural HP nor a reviewed improvement option, retain Standard output and the quality label only. Consumables do not gain reusable doses or longer durations from this generic option.

A quantity-1 Flawed durable item has maximum structural HP equal to half its ordinary maximum, rounded down, minimum 1, and begins at that reduced maximum. This reduced maximum is a crafting flaw, not ordinary structural damage. Ordinary equipment repair may restore current structural HP only up to that reduced maximum; it does not remove the flaw, increase the item's maximum, alter its equipment grade or convert it to Standard quality. Removing a crafting flaw requires an explicit reviewed rework procedure; absent one, the reduced maximum persists. A quantity-1 consumable whose useful effect has a positive finite duration instead has half that duration, rounded down to a whole round (six seconds), minimum one round. Instant healing/damage/RP restoration and otherwise incompatible results have no generic flaw profile: treat that Flawed result as Failed with the normal 25% non-catalyst recovery. Do not halve an undefined feature or invent a permanent debuff. The completed output card must state whether either default applies.

Masterwork preserves **one component unit total** bearing role catalyst and consumed=true, chosen after the check. It must be an actual catalyst used in this batch, not a named irreplaceable component whose exact formula requires destruction; an indivisible catalyst cannot be split. Return that unit to inventory unchanged rather than deducting it. With no eligible catalyst, nothing is returned. The ingredient's exact identity, tier and remaining shelf life persist; this is not a fresh item. Nonconsumed tools always remain unless a specific mishap physically damages one.

**Reviewed Forge Dwarf completion:** when eligible artisan-tool creation achieves Standard, treat its output as Exceptional for the yield/improvement choice. Already Exceptional/Masterwork remains so. Failed, Flawed and Mishap do not upgrade. This gives the ancestry's quality language a bounded crafting function; it grants no equipment grade, price multiplier, success guarantee or extra XP.

## Mishaps

The public source references a tradeskill mishap table but contains none. **Completion:** after losing consumed inputs, roll 1d6 on this shared table. The trade reference supplies the injury damage type, giving every trade an executable table. A Mishap still never destroys a formula or an irreplaceable tool unless the damage below actually reduces that tool to 0 HP. Cleanup/calibration time is extra active time after the failed batch, not part of its completion hours.

| d6 | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | Spilled workspace: 1 active hour of cleanup before this station can be used again. |
| 2 | Miscalibration: the primary kit cannot support another crafting check until someone proficient with it spends 2 active hours recalibrating it. No extra ingredients are required. |
