blocks.text: Chapter 36 — Rival Expeditions and Faction Turns

Rivals make the Opening move when the player characters are not looking. They are most effective when they are competent, understandable, and capable of cooperation as well as betrayal. A rival that exists only to steal kills or mock the party will become tedious. A rival with overlapping goals creates decisions.

rows: Line they claim they will not cross
What they need from the party
What they fear the party will learn

blocks.text: Give a rival one thing it does better than the player Expedition and one thing it does worse. The Gilded Wake may have superior funding and weak field discipline. The Ashen Lanterns may map brilliantly but lack healing. This creates credible exchanges and prevents rivals from feeling like omnipotent Director avatars.

After each return to a haven or the surface, choose up to three watched factions. Each takes one action: recruit, denounce, buy, raid, research, fortify, bargain, conceal, or wait. Resolve the action at the level players can perceive. A faction may advance a private project, but the next session should contain a rumor, price shift, messenger, missing person, new guard presence, or other visible sign.

rows: Time passes, the party shares maps, or the rival gains support
Rival reaches a contested node or Gate
Rival gathers proof, witnesses, or legal support
Rival controls salvage, route, or public credit
Humiliation, loss, betrayal, or public accusation
Rival acts directly against the party
Casualties, debt, internal conflict, or exposure
Rival fractures, bargains desperately, or becomes dangerous

blocks.text: Let rivals achieve objectives. Their victories prove the world is moving and create new situations: the route is open but taxed, the relic is already sold, a Gate has been disturbed, or a rival survivor needs rescue. Do not erase the player campaign. A rival victory changes the objective rather than making play irrelevant.

rows: Rivals Know Only What They Could Learn

Do not use rival Expeditions to deliver Director knowledge, perfectly counter player plans, or appear wherever the story needs friction. Track their routes, information sources, and time. Fair rivals are more threatening because players can understand how they succeeded.

blocks.text: Chapter 44 — Social Conflict and Reputation Scenes

A social scene becomes a conflict when someone wants an outcome the other side has reason to resist. Roleplay determines approach and information; checks resolve uncertainty. Reputation determines the starting field and what outcomes are plausible. A Honored Expedition may be heard without an appointment. A Hated one may need leverage merely to enter the room.

rows: What does each side want before the scene ends?
What can each side offer, reveal, threaten, or withhold?
What will each side not agree to under current conditions?
What changes if the conversation takes too long?
Who will hear about the outcome?

blocks.text: Prepare a full success, costly success, and refusal or reversal. Costly success is not a disguised failure; the party gets the requested access or agreement but owes a favor, accepts oversight, loses secrecy, pays more, or grants credit. Refusal should open another path: new leverage, a different faction, illegal entry, or delayed opportunity.

Persuasion changes willingness, Deception changes believed information, Intimidation changes perceived risk, and Insight changes what the character understands. No single skill controls another person’s mind. A perfect argument cannot make an NPC betray the one value the scene established as non-negotiable, though it may reveal what would change that limit.

Move reputation after actions that are public, significant, and attributable. Private kindness may change one NPC without changing a faction. A witnessed Gate victory, broken treaty, rescue, theft, or public accusation can shift a tier. Record why the movement occurred; later NPCs should react to the story, not the number alone.

Your Reputation reflects how you are perceived by the various factions, settlements, and influential figures across Aethel. It is a dynamic score, influenced by your background, actions, alignment, and affiliations. High reputation with a group can unlock quests, provide discounts, grant access to restricted areas, or earn you valuable allies. Conversely, low reputation can lead to hostility, suspicion, increased prices, or outright refusal of service.
Starting Reputation: Your chosen Background often provides a starting positive or negative reputation with specific groups relevant to your past.

Gaining/Losing Reputation: Completing quests, making significant choices, demonstrating your alignment through actions (helping the needy vs. exploiting the weak), associating with certain NPCs, and even succeeding or failing certain social skill checks can all modify your reputation scores with various factions.
Reputation Tiers: Reputation often functions in tiers (e.g., Hated, Disliked, Neutral, Liked, Honored), with each tier unlocking different interactions and consequences.

Alignment Influence: Actions consistent with your alignment tend to improve reputation with like-minded factions and decrease it with opposing ones. A Good character consistently acting selflessly will gain reputation with temples and righteous orders but lose it with thieves' guilds or dark cults.
Managing your reputation is crucial for navigating the complex social and political landscape of Aethel.

A Charisma check might arise when you try to influence or entertain others, when you try to make an impression or tell a convincing lie, or when you are navigating a tricky social situation. The Deception, Intimidation, Performance, Persuasion, and Reputation skills reflect aptitude in certain kinds of Charisma checks.

Deception. Your Charisma (Deception) check determines whether you can convincingly hide the truth, either verbally or through your actions. This deception can encompass everything from misleading others through ambiguity to telling outright lies. Typical situations include trying to fast-talk a guard, con a merchant, earn money through gambling, pass yourself off in a disguise, dull someone's suspicions with false assurances, or maintain a straight face while telling a blatant lie.

Intimidation. When you attempt to influence someone through overt threats, hostile actions, and physical violence, the Director might ask you to make a Charisma (Intimidation) check. Examples include trying to pry information out of a prisoner, convincing street thugs to back down from a confrontation, or using the edge of a broken bottle to convince a sneering noble to reconsider a decision.
Performance. Your Charisma (Performance) check determines how well you can delight an audience with music, dance, acting, storytelling, or some other form of entertainment.

Persuasion. When you attempt to influence someone or a group of people with tact, social graces, or good nature, the Director might ask you to make a Charisma (Persuasion) check. Typically, you use persuasion when acting in good faith, to foster friendships, make cordial requests, or exhibit proper etiquette. Examples of persuading others include convincing a chamberlain to let your party see the king, negotiating peace between warring tribes, or inspiring a crowd of townsfolk.

Reputation. Your Charisma (Reputation) check reflects how well you can leverage your standing with various factions and communities throughout Aethel. This might involve calling in favors, being recognized for past deeds, or using your influence to open doors that would otherwise remain closed.
Other Charisma Checks. The Director might call for a Charisma check when you try to accomplish tasks like the following:
* Find the best person to talk to for news, rumors, and gossip
* Blend into a crowd to get the sense of key topics of conversation
In Decennium Descent, your character's reputation with various factions and their alignment can significantly impact ability checks in social situations.
When interacting with NPCs affiliated with specific factions, your reputation level with that faction can provide bonuses or penalties to Charisma-based ability checks:
* Revered (+5): You're a legendary figure to this faction
Your alignment relative to an NPC's alignment can also affect social interactions:

Remember that Good and Evil alignments are fundamentally incompatible in Aethel, while Harmony and Discord can work together despite tension. Neutral characters can bridge these divides, serving as mediators between opposing forces.
These reputation and alignment systems add depth to social encounters in Aethel, making your character's standing in the world and moral choices mechanically significant beyond combat situations.

boons.name: Curse Boon I
boons.description: Spectral attendants grant +1 AC against the first attack each round. Once per day, a spirit whispers a warning — you cannot be surprised.

boons.name: Curse Boon II
boons.description: Once per combat, a bound spirit intercepts a single-target attack against you, absorbing up to 5 + level damage before dissipating. The spirit wails as it fades — the attacker must save or suffer −2 to their next attack as dread clings to them.

boons.name: Curse Boon III
boons.description: Spirits murmur of danger — you and allies within 3 tiles cannot be surprised while you are conscious. Echoes of the dead grant +2 to Insight checks nearby.

boons.name: Curse Boon IV
boons.description: Summon a wailing chorus: enemies within 3 tiles suffer Dread (−10% hit chance and saves) for 2 turns. Once per long rest.

boons.name: Curse Boon V
boons.description: Once per day, bind a hostile or friendly spirit to scout, speak with the dead at a distance, or deliver a prophetic message along a path you have walked. The spirit persists for 10 minutes or until it completes one task; when it returns, it whispers what it saw and one name you did not send it to find.

card.name: False Life
card.effect: LIMITATIONS: divination treats you as undead unless it specifically pierces Oracle curses. Before a healing spell from another creature restores HP to you, its caster may make Wisdom (Insight) against your Revelation save DC. On success healing works normally. On failure roll d2; on 1 the spell restores 0 HP to you but still expends its normal costs. Non-spell healing is unaffected. Social hesitation from life-focused clergy remains narrative unless the scene calls for an ordinary reaction check.

value.name: False Life
value.blurb: Magic mistakes your living breath for death and answers accordingly
limitations: Healing spells cast on you without a successful Insight check have a 50% chance to fail; magic reads you as corpse-cold
Unless you suppress the curse, divination treats you as undead
Clerics of life-deities may hesitate to aid you without proof that you still breathe

boons.name: Curse Boon I
boons.description: Advantage on saves vs death effects and negative energy. Once per long rest, when you would die, stabilize at 1 HP as your body feigns death perfectly.

boons.name: Curse Boon II
boons.description: Feign death perfectly for 1 minute — undead ignore you unless attacked; you remain conscious but motionless. Once per combat.

boons.name: Curse Boon III
boons.description: When reduced to 0 HP, remain conscious for 1 round before falling — you may move, speak, or cast one Revelation. Once per long rest.

boons.name: Curse Boon IV
boons.description: Necrotic resilience: +10% DR vs necrotic and negative energy. Undead attackers have 10% chance to miss you entirely, sensing kinship.

boons.name: Curse Boon V
boons.description: Once per day, return from death's threshold — after 1 round of appearing dead at 0 HP, rise at 25% max HP with immunity to necrotic for 2 rounds. Undead within 3 tiles treat you as kin until you act, and divination cast during your feigned death returns false results of your choosing.

card.effect: once per short rest reroll a failed Intelligence or Wisdom ability check and use the new result; gain +2 on Insight checks made to read motives.

value.name: Shattered Mind
value.blurb: Your thoughts divide into competing fragments that act before they agree
limitations: Concentration checks are at −2 as competing thoughts contend for control
In tense social scenes, make a Wisdom save or speak a prophetic fragment aloud on an impulse not wholly your own
After a long rest, make a Wisdom save or wake with fragmented memories of others' dreams

boons.name: Curse Boon I
boons.description: Once per combat, take a bonus move or activate one Tier I Revelation as a bonus action (not both a full action and bonus action in the same turn). The fragment acting is not wholly yours — observers may hear you answer questions you were never asked.

boons.name: Curse Boon II
boons.description: Fragmented focus: +2 initiative; immune to being stunned. Your initiative roll may be made twice — take the higher result.

boons.name: Curse Boon III
boons.description: Split thought: maintain two Revelation effects simultaneously for 1 round without paying double charges. Once per combat.

boons.name: Curse Boon IV
boons.description: Mind echo: reroll one failed Intelligence or Wisdom check per short rest. Prophetic fragments grant +2 to Insight when reading motives.

boons.name: Curse Boon V
boons.description: Once per day, act twice in a single round — second action may be a Revelation or move only. Each action uses a different fragment of your mind.

card.name: Ancestral Whispers
card.effect: Gain advantage on History checks and you cannot be Surprised while conscious. Once per long rest, spend 1 minute consulting your ancestors about one specific person, place, object or course of action. The Director provides one truthful cryptic clue drawn from knowledge the ancestral spirits could reasonably possess; they do not reveal unknowable future decisions.

value.name: Ancestral Whispers
value.description: Advantage on History checks and immunity to surprise. Once per day, consult ancestors for cryptic but useful guidance.

card.name: Echo Crowned
card.cost: 0 RC to maintain spirits; Revelation costs normally unless stated
card.rangeAndTarget: Self; death prevention ally within 5 tiles
card.frequency: Double-cast 1/long rest; each spirit may be sacrificed once per long rest
card.effect: Maintain three named ancestral Echoes: Offense grants +1 on your first Revelation attack each round; Defense reduces the first damage you take each round by S; Utility grants advantage on one History, Insight or Perception check per round. Once per long rest, when you activate a known Revelation, you may pay its RC cost twice and resolve it twice as part of the same action against different legal targets; copied resolution cannot duplicate resource or action triggers. You may sacrifice one currently available Echo as a Reaction when an ally within 5 tiles would be reduced to 0 HP to leave that ally at 1 HP instead, or as a Bonus Action to restore your RC to maximum. A sacrificed Echo provides no passive benefit until your next long rest.

value.name: Echo Crowned
value.description: Maintain 3 passive ancestral spirits (offense, defense, utility). Once per day, cast any Revelation twice in one turn using different Echoes. Sacrifice an Echo to prevent a party member's death or restore all Revelation Charges.

card.name: Battle-Seer's Eye
card.duration: Permanent; AC benefit against one attack
card.effect: Gain advantage on Perception and initiative rolls. Once per long rest when a visible enemy declares an attack against you or an ally within 5 tiles, use your Reaction before the roll; you and one ally within 5 tiles gain +2 AC against that enemy's next attack before the end of its current turn.

value.name: Battle-Seer's Eye
value.description: Advantage on Perception and Initiative. Once per day, foretell an enemy's opening strike — you and one ally gain +2 AC against that enemy's next attack.

card.name: Ledger's Memory
card.effect: Gain advantage on checks to identify undead, poison and disease. Once per long rest, touch one corpse and learn its identity if the Pale Ledger could reasonably know it, its approximate time of death and the direct physical or magical cause of death. This does not reveal the killer's identity unless the corpse or supernatural Ledger actually knows it.

value.name: Ledger's Memory
value.description: Advantage on checks to identify undead, poison, and disease. Once per day, consult the Pale Ledger for the name and cause of death of any corpse you touch.

card.name: Wound of Creation
card.effect: Gain advantage on checks involving geology, storms, earthquakes, structural stability and unstable terrain. Once per long rest spend an Action to sense the nearest significant structural weak point, unstable surface, hidden fracture or likely collapse point within 10 tiles that is physically connected to your surroundings. You learn direction and broad nature, not an automatic method to destroy it.

value.name: Wound of Creation
value.description: Advantage on checks involving geology, storms, or the Descent's unstable floors. Once per day, sense the nearest structural weak point within 10 tiles.

card.name: Lucid Oracle
card.effect: Gain advantage on saves against magical sleep and Illusion effects. Once per long rest spend 10 minutes asking the Veiled Threshold one specific question concerning the present situation or a contemplated course of action. Receive one truthful symbolic vision or omen. It cannot reveal another player's unknowable future choice.

value.name: Lucid Oracle
value.description: Advantage on saves vs sleep and illusion. Once per day, ask the Veiled Threshold one question — receive a symbolic but truthful vision.

card.name: Founder's Memory
card.effect: Gain advantage on History checks involving Tyrnathar, the Crown of First Flame and the Tenfold Cycles. Once per long rest after failing a saving throw against fire damage or Frightened, reroll that save and use the new result.

value.name: Founder's Memory
value.description: Advantage on History checks involving Tyrnathar and the Tenfold Cycles. Once per day, invoke the Crown's memory to reroll a failed save vs fire or fear.

card.name: Bloom Oracle
card.frequency: Skill benefit always; supernatural diagnosis 1/long rest
card.effect: Gain advantage on Medicine and Nature checks. Once per long rest, examine one willing creature for 1 minute and learn the broad nature of one disease, poison, curse-like affliction or bodily condition affecting it plus one plausible mundane, magical or quest-based countermeasure known to the Verdant Resonance. This identifies rather than automatically cures the condition.

value.name: Bloom Oracle
value.description: Advantage on Medicine and Nature. Once per day, diagnose any affliction by touch and learn one countermeasure the Verdant Resonance suggests.

card.name: Shadow Oracle
card.rangeAndTarget: Self; one creature within 3 tiles that you can perceive
card.frequency: Skill benefits always; fear reading 1/long rest
card.effect: Gain advantage on Stealth and Insight checks. Once per long rest choose one creature within 3 tiles and spend an Action reading its surface fear. If the creature is not protected from mind-reading or divination, the Director truthfully identifies one present fear, dread or aversion known to that creature. This grants information only and does not compel behavior.

value.name: Shadow Oracle
value.description: Advantage on Stealth and Insight. Once per day, read the hidden fear in one creature's heart — learn their greatest dread (DM provides truthful answer).

card.name: Stellar Oracle
card.effect: Gain advantage on checks involving astronomy, astrology and navigation. Once per long rest spend 10 minutes reading the sky or a divination focus concerning one specific party decision. The Director supplies one truthful but cryptic omen about a likely consequence known to the Celestial Concord. It cannot dictate another player's future decision or guarantee an outcome.

value.name: Stellar Oracle
value.description: Advantage on Astrology and Navigation. Once per day, read the sky (or a divination focus) for cryptic guidance on a party decision.

card.name: Spiral Oracle
card.effect: Gain advantage on checks involving history, prophecy and the Tenfold Cycles. Once per long rest spend 10 minutes asking whether one specific contemplated action is likely to provoke a serious foreseeable disaster within the next day. The Director answers yes, no or unclear and provides one cryptic truthful hint. This does not reveal player choices or guarantee a deterministic future.

value.name: Spiral Oracle
value.description: Advantage on checks involving history, prophecy, or the Tenfold Cycles. Once per day, ask the Turning Spiral whether a specific action will provoke disaster (yes/no with cryptic hint).

card.name: No Escape
card.rangeAndTarget: Up to 3 creatures marked by you within 60 feet
card.effect: While affected, a marked creature cannot voluntarily teleport, become invisible or enter extradimensional travel. If it willingly moves out of your Oath aura, opportunity attacks against it have advantage until the end of its next turn. This spell does not prevent ordinary movement, forced movement or planar effects explicitly stronger than the ward.

value.spell: No Escape — marked foes within 60 ft cannot teleport, become invisible, or use extradimensional travel; if they leave your aura, opportunity attacks against them have advantage until end of next turn

card.name: Aura of Authority
card.rangeAndTarget: Up to 3 chosen creatures in your Oath aura
card.duration: While conscious and target remains in aura
card.frequency: Choose targets at start of each turn
card.effect: A selected ally gains +1 on Intimidation checks. When a selected hostile creature knowingly attempts to speak a direct falsehood, it makes a Charisma save. On failure the lie catches in its voice and listeners know supernatural pressure disrupted the statement, but the creature is never forced to answer truthfully and may instead stop speaking.

originalObjects.value: Aura of Authority — allies +1 to Intimidation; enemies must save to lie within aura

card.name: Heaven's Decree
card.rangeAndTarget: One creature within 30 feet that can hear you
card.duration: Until end of target's next turn
card.effect: State one simple command: Approach, Retreat, Drop, Kneel, Halt or Release. The target makes a Wisdom save. On failure, at the start of its next turn it chooses either follow the command in the safest reasonable way using no more than movement and one object interaction, or refuse and take 3 S d6 psychic damage. Player-controlled targets always make this choice themselves. The command cannot require self-harm, confession, belief change or permanent allegiance.

originalObjects.value: Heaven's Decree — command obey or suffer psychic damage (1/rest)

card.name: Sovereign's Ascendance
card.rangeAndTarget: Up to 3 creatures in your Oath aura
card.effect: Choose up to 3 creatures in your aura. An allied target gains advantage on Charisma saves and +2 on Intimidation checks for 3 rounds. A hostile target immediately receives Heaven's Decree without an initial save and must choose whether to obey its bounded command or take the normal psychic backlash. Until the end of its next turn it also cannot knowingly speak a direct falsehood in your presence. This Final does not permit self-harm commands, forced belief, confession or permanent allegiance.

originalObjects.value: Sovereign's Ascendance — once per day, Heaven's Decree affects all enemies in aura without save; allies gain advantage on Charisma saves and +2 to Intimidation for 3 rounds, and enemies who fail cannot lie or disobey a direct command until end of next turn.

completeEnvelope.protectedInterfaceOriginal: Once per turn, spending 2 or more Conviction on a Rite or Invocation vents 1 Dissonance; prayer changes cadence instead of bypassing Resonance.
engine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Wisdom is the Cleric class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Cleric levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Wisdom modifier) unless a feature explicitly substitutes another ability. Cleric technique attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Wisdom modifier. Cleric technique save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Wisdom modifier.

Conviction is separate from Resonance Points. Base Conviction maximum is 3, automatically becoming 5 at Cleric 9; after a long rest you begin at your current maximum. A completed short rest restores 1 spent Conviction, to the maximum. A completed long rest restores all Conviction. Conviction Pool raises the maximum by 2. Conviction persists between encounters; simply declaring prayer, repeating a Rite, or performing harmless actions outside a real encounter never generates Conviction.

Only explicit features generate Conviction. Sacred Chant, Sermon of Purpose, Doctrine Shield, Dark Conviction and other printed cards are valid generators. A feature cannot generate more Conviction than its text permits, and Conviction can never exceed the current maximum. Summoned creatures, friendly creatures, trivial creatures, repeated corpse manipulation and staged out-of-combat actions cannot be used to farm Conviction.

Cleric techniques use only their printed RP and Conviction costs. All RP is paid from the Cleric's Core Systems V 2 Resonance Point pool. A Cleric technique is not automatically an ordinary spell-rank cast and does not receive Overcast, spell-slot, cost-discount or spell-proc benefits unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Ordinary spells continue to use Core V 2 spellcasting rules.

Protected Dissonance interaction: once on each of your regular turns, when you spend at least 2 Conviction on a Rite or Invocation, reduce Dissonance by 1, minimum 0. The expenditure must actually occur; waived Conviction costs do not vent Dissonance. A single feature expenditure vents at most once even if it spends more than 2 Conviction. No Cleric card automatically adds Dissonance unless explicitly written.

One concentration effect may be maintained at a time. Starting another concentration effect immediately ends the previous one. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; for this pilot, if a division requires rounding, half damage is rounded down. Sustained Cleric effects use their printed maintenance cost and Bonus Action. A control effect that persists for multiple pulses or rounds gives the target a new save at each printed pulse or at the end of each affected turn as stated.

Round recharge counters are set after resolution and decrease once at the start of the Cleric's regular initiative turn, even if the Cleric cannot act. Extra Actions and extra turns do not create extra recharge ticks. Outside initiative, each uninterrupted 6 seconds counts as one recharge tick. Only a positive counter may be reset or shortened, and a named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

Healing cannot exceed maximum HP, does not remove Wounds, and does not restore a dead creature unless a card explicitly says it resurrects. No Cleric feature provides unlimited permanent HP or resource restoration outside encounters. Temporary HP does not stack with itself; use the higher value. Resurrection and corpse-based effects have explicit use limits and cannot generate repeatable corpses, XP, loot or Conviction.

Invocation Attunement is gained automatically at Cleric level 2. Choose exactly one Invocation Path: Radiance, Judgment, Renewal, Flame, Veil or Echoes. Only the selected path bonus becomes active. Divine Invocation uses the mode belonging to that selected path unless another feature explicitly permits a different mode. Changing Invocation Path requires a future explicit retraining rule; this draft provides none.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION FOR PLAYTEST. Cleric 1: gain the Divine Favor engine and choose 4 Base cards, at least 2 Active. Cleric 2: automatically gain Invocation Attunement and the selected Invocation Path bonus, then choose 2 additional Base cards. Cleric 3: enter Bishop and choose 2 Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Levels 4-8 each grant one eligible Base/Arch choice, respecting each card's minimum class level. Level 9 grants one eligible Arch choice plus Bishop's Mandate automatically. Level 10 choose Saint, Priest or Cultist and gain 2 Hero choices from that path. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one additional Hero choice; levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch choice. The chosen Hero Finale is automatic at Cleric 20. ASI/feat milestones remain separate and do not consume these choices.

All acquisition gates use Cleric class level, not total character level. Proficiency bonus still follows normal total-character-level rules. A multiclass character cannot use non-Cleric levels to unlock Bishop, Hero, Invocation or Finale features. Divine commands, visions and social abilities can influence actions only to the extent their exact mechanical text states; no Cleric feature can force a player character to adopt, abandon or profess a belief.

Capacity clarification: the automatic level 9 Conviction increase is a new draft completion so every Hero can pay its 5-Conviction Finale without buying Conviction Pool. Conviction Pool adds 2 at any level, yielding 5 early or 7 from 9. It never fills gained capacity immediately.
workedExample: Cleric 5 example: Wisdom 16 gives M=3, PB=3, S=2. Assume the Core V 2 sheet gives this test Cleric 12 RP. The Cleric knows Conviction Pool, so maximum Conviction is 5, begins the encounter at Conviction 5, Dissonance 3, and selected Judgment at level 2.

Turn 1: Divine Smite costs 1 Conviction, so Conviction 5→4 and RP remains 12. On a hit it deals 2d8+3 radiant damage. Judgment automatically marks the target Judged for 2 rounds, giving it -1 AC. Spending only 1 Conviction does not vent Dissonance.

Turn 2: Divine Invocation costs 2 Conviction and 3 RP, so Conviction 4→2 and RP 12→9. Because an Invocation spent at least 2 Conviction, Dissonance vents once, 3→2. Using Judgment mode, a failed Wisdom save causes the printed 3d8 radiant effect and refreshes Judged.

Turn 3: Healing Rite costs 2 RP, so RP 9→7. It restores 2d8+3 HP to one living ally. It spends no Conviction, so Conviction remains 2 and Dissonance remains 2. If the ally stood in the Cleric's Consecrate zone and Consecrated Ground was known, the target would also regain the printed S=2 bonus HP.
Turn 4: Sacred Chant costs 1 RP to start, so RP 7→6. Its first pulse occurs, but generates no Conviction yet. The Cleric concentrates on the Chant. Conviction stays 2.

Turn 5: The Cleric maintains Sacred Chant with a Bonus Action. Because Sermon of Purpose is known, the second pulse generates 1 Conviction, 2→3. The Cleric then uses Divine Smite as the normal Action, spending 1 Conviction, 3→2. RP remains 6 and Dissonance remains 2 because no single Rite or Invocation expenditure of at least 2 Conviction occurred this turn.
balanceQuestions: Does a 3-point base Conviction cap, or 5 with Conviction Pool, create meaningful expenditure choices without making Sacred Chant mandatory in every encounter?
Do Bishop's Mandate, Miraculous Channel and the six Invocation modes create excessive burst or action compression when combined, especially at levels 7-10?

Across Saint, Priest and Cultist, are healing, control, resurrection and Conviction regeneration sufficiently bounded across multiple encounters without making ordinary Core V2 spellcasting irrelevant?

source.originalText: Miraculous Channel: Sacrificing 3 Conviction causes your next Rite to affect the full party.

cards.name: Bishop's Mandate
cards.rangeAndTarget: Your Sacrament and one legal Divine Invocation target set
cards.frequency: Automatic at Cleric 9; once per Sacrament start
cards.effect: Bishop's Mandate. Tags: sacrament, invocation, capstone. When you legally start Sacrament, immediately resolve one free Divine Invocation using your selected Invocation Path. This free Invocation requires no Action, RP or Conviction, sets no Divine Invocation recharge and cannot itself trigger Bishop's Mandate. The Sacrament's own Conviction expenditure may still vent Dissonance normally.

source.originalText: Capstone: Bishop's Mandate: Activating a Sacrament automatically casts a free Invocation without cost or cooldown.

cards.name: Divine Invocation
cards.effect: Divine Invocation. Tags: invocation, bishop. Use only your selected Invocation Path. Radiance: up to 3 allies within 30 feet each regain S d8+M HP; one may end Frightened or Poisoned. Judgment: one enemy within 60 feet makes a Wisdom save, taking (S+1)d8 radiant on failure or half on success; failure also applies Judged for 2 rounds. Renewal: up to 2 allies within 30 feet each regain S d8+M HP and 5 Stamina. Flame: creatures in a 15-foot cone make Dexterity saves, taking (S+1)d8 fire on failure or half on success; failed targets also take 1d6 fire at the start of their next turn. Veil: up to 3 allies within 30 feet can see invisible/ethereal creatures within 30 feet and gain advantage on saves against illusions for 3 rounds. Echoes: choose one eligible Smite or Rite you resolved this turn or previous regular turn and one original target within 30 feet; repeat 50% of its immediate unmodified rolled damage or healing dice, rounded down once, minimum 1 for a positive source, with no copied conditions, resources or triggers.

source.originalText: Divine Invocation: Channel a powerful prayer based on your chosen Invocation Path, with effects ranging from mass healing to divine fire or protective barriers.

cards.name: Sacrament
cards.cost: 3 Conviction + 4 RP to start; 1 RP maintenance
cards.effect: Sacrament. Tags: sacrament, rite, sustained, zone. Pulse on start and on each paid Bonus Action maintenance. At each pulse, up to three allies in the zone gain +1 on saving throws until the start of your next regular turn or effect end, whichever is first. Up to three Undead or Fiends in the zone make Wisdom saves, taking S d6 radiant damage on failure or half on success. Maximum 3 pulses.

source.originalText: Sacrament: Perform a sacred ceremony that consumes Conviction to create a powerful, sustained effect in an area.

cards.name: Banish Unholy
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to three Undead or Fiends within 30 feet
cards.duration: Instantaneous; banishment rider lasts until end of target's next turn
cards.effect: Banish Unholy. Tags: divine, control. Each target makes a Wisdom save. Failure deals (S+1)d8 radiant damage and pushes it up to 15 feet directly away from you; success takes half damage and no push. A target failing by 10 or more is also banished until the end of its next turn, then returns to the nearest legal space.

source.originalText: Banish Unholy: Channel divine energy to damage and potentially banish undead, demons, or other unholy entities.

cards.name: Blessing of Protection
cards.effect: Blessing of Protection. Tags: blessing, protection. Choose one mode on use. Resistance: choose acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, radiant or thunder; the ally gains resistance to that damage type. Resolve: choose Charmed, Frightened or Poisoned; the ally gains advantage on saves against that condition and may immediately repeat one current save against it.

source.originalText: Blessing of Protection:  Bestow a divine blessing on an ally, granting them resistance to a specific damage type or condition.

cards.name: Commune
cards.effect: Commune. Tags: ritual, information, bishop. Ask up to three questions concerning divine doctrine, sacred duties, supernatural threats or a course of action. For each, the Director answers truthfully with yes, no, unclear or a brief symbolic response based on what the contacted divine source could know. Commune cannot compel a deity, reveal another player's private belief, or guarantee a future choice.

source.originalText: Commune:  Enter a deep meditative state to receive guidance directly from your deity, gaining insight on important matters or divine intervention.

cards.name: Aura of Grace
cards.frequency: Healing once/own regular turn; critical reduction once/ally/round
cards.effect: Aura of Grace. At the start of your regular turn during a real encounter, you may pay 1 RP to heal S HP to up to 3 living allies within 15 ft below half maximum HP. You must be conscious. Separately, once per ally per round when an ally in the aura suffers a critical hit, reduce its added critical damage by one damage die, minimum 0 extra dice. No unlimited free healing.

source.originalText: Aura of Grace: Allies in range resist critical hits and gain minor HP regen.

cards.name: Divine Rebirth
cards.rangeAndTarget: One ally revived by your Cleric feature
cards.duration: Instantaneous plus temporary HP for 1 minute
cards.effect: Divine Rebirth. Tags: saint, resurrection. When one of your Cleric features returns an ally from death, you may use Divine Rebirth. That ally returns with half its maximum HP instead of the feature's normal returned HP and gains S + M temporary HP for 1 minute. It removes no Wounds and cannot affect a creature that was not actually dead.

source.originalText: Divine Rebirth: On revive, ally returns with 50% HP and a temporary resistance shield.

cards.name: Merciful Sacrament
cards.effect: Merciful Sacrament. Tags: saint, sacrament. When you start Sacrament and at least one living ally inside its initial zone is at or below one-quarter maximum HP, you may reduce that Sacrament's Conviction cost to 0. Its RP cost and all other requirements remain. Because no Conviction is spent, this waived cost does not vent Dissonance.

source.originalText: Merciful Sacrament: Sacraments cost no Conviction if used on an ally under 25% HP.

cards.name: Unyielding Light
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to six living party members within 30 feet, including you
cards.effect: Unyielding Light. Tags: saint, emergency, healing. When one damage event would leave every conscious living party member within 30 feet at 0 HP, resolve that damage, then before ordinary death-save progression each qualifying living creature at 0 HP regains floor(maximum HP/3), minimum 1. It cannot revive a creature killed outright and removes no Wounds. This one emergency trigger may resolve even if that event incapacitates you, provided you remain alive; it grants no other actions while incapacitated.

source.originalText: Unyielding Light: Once per day, prevents party wipe and restores 30% HP.

cards.name: Celestial Resurgence
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to six allied corpses within 30 feet that died during the previous 3 rounds
cards.effect: Final Miracle — Celestial Resurgence. Tags: saint, finale, resurrection, rite. Each legal target returns to life at 1 HP. The body must be sufficiently present to sustain life. This removes no Wounds, curses or other death consequences. Divine Rebirth may modify one returned ally if available. The Conviction expenditure can vent Dissonance once under the common rule.

source.originalText: Final Miracle: Celestial Resurgence: Revive all allies who died within the last 3 turns.

cards.name: Mass Healing Light
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to six living allies within 30 feet
cards.effect: Mass Healing Light. Tags: saint, healing. Roll S d8 + M once. Each target regains that amount. A target below half maximum HP when chosen regains an additional 1d8 HP. Roll that bonus once and apply it to all qualifying targets. This cannot revive the dead or remove Wounds.

source.originalText: Mass Healing Light: Channel divine energy to heal all allies within 30 feet, with increased effectiveness on those most wounded.

cards.name: Divine Intervention
cards.effect: Divine Intervention. Tags: saint, emergency. Trigger when the ally either fails a saving throw or takes damage that would reduce it to 0 HP. Choose one: the ally rerolls the failed save and must use the new result; or reduce the triggering damage by 2 S d8 + M, minimum 0. This cannot negate an event that has already fully resolved.

source.originalText: Divine Intervention: Call upon your deity to intervene directly, potentially averting disaster or creating a miraculous effect.

cards.name: Sanctify Being
cards.effect: Sanctify Being. Tags: saint, protection. Choose one mode. Elemental Sanctity grants resistance to one of acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, radiant or thunder. Purity grants immunity to exactly one of Charmed, Frightened or Poisoned. Choose when activated; the choice cannot change during that use.

source.originalText: Sanctify Being: Bestow temporary divine protection on an ally, granting them immunity to specific conditions or damage types.

cards.name: Radiant Burst
cards.rangeAndTarget: 15-foot radius centered on you; up to six allies and six Undead/Fiends
cards.effect: Radiant Burst. Tags: saint, healing, radiant. Roll S d8 once. Each chosen living ally regains that roll + M HP. Each chosen Undead or Fiend makes a Wisdom save, taking the same S d8 roll as radiant damage on failure or half on success. Healing and damage are separate applications of the shared roll.

source.originalText: Radiant Burst: Release a powerful wave of divine energy that heals allies and damages unholy creatures.

cards.name: Resurrection
cards.rangeAndTarget: One allied corpse you touch that died within the previous 1 minute
cards.effect: Resurrection. Tags: saint, resurrection, rite. Return the target to life at 1 HP and grant it 2 S + M temporary HP for 1 minute. It gains no removed Wounds and receives no restored expended resources beyond what another rule explicitly provides. A missing vital body prevents the effect. The Conviction expenditure can vent Dissonance once.

source.originalText: Resurrection: Return a fallen ally to life with renewed vigor and temporary divine blessing.

cards.name: Scriptural Echo
cards.rangeAndTarget: One legal original target of your previously used Divine Invocation
cards.effect: Scriptural Echo. Tags: priest, rite, invocation. When you start a Rite, you may repeat 50% of the immediate rolled damage or healing dice from the most recent Divine Invocation you personally resolved since the end of your previous regular turn. Round down once, minimum 1 for a positive source. It copies no conditions, movement, resource effects, control or Invocation Path triggers.

source.originalText: Scriptural Echo: Casting a Rite repeats the Invocation used previously for 50% effect.

cards.name: Words of Equilibrium
cards.effect: Words of Equilibrium. Tags: priest, scaling. For numeric Cleric technique healing and damage that would add your Wisdom modifier, use the higher of your Intelligence or Wisdom modifier instead. M becomes max(1, that higher modifier) for those numeric effects. This does not change Cleric attack rolls or save DCs unless another rule explicitly says so.

source.originalText: Words of Equilibrium: Heal and Damage dealt scale off the higher of INT or WIS.

cards.name: Balanced Scales
cards.rangeAndTarget: Living creatures healed by your Cleric features
cards.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
cards.frequency: At most once per marked ally per round
cards.effect: Balanced Scales. Tags: priest, healing, retaliation. After you restore HP to a living ally, mark it until the start of your next regular turn. The first enemy to damage that ally during the mark takes S + M radiant damage. The retaliation is not an attack, cannot critically hit and cannot recursively trigger another Balanced Scales event.

source.originalText: Balanced Scales: Enemies take divine damage if they attack healed targets.

cards.name: Doctrine Shield
cards.effect: Doctrine Shield. Tags: priest, conviction, cleanse. During a real encounter, when one of your Cleric features successfully removes Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned or another explicitly removable condition from a living creature, gain 1 Conviction. Removing multiple conditions in the same event still grants only 1 Conviction.

source.originalText: Doctrine Shield: Gain 1 Conviction anytime a condition is removed.

cards.name: Word of Binding
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to six enemies within 30 feet
cards.effect: Final Miracle — Word of Binding. Tags: priest, finale, control, rite. Each target makes a Wisdom save. On failure it is Silenced and its Speed becomes 0. At the end of each of its turns it repeats the save, ending both effects on success. While a target remains bound, the first instance of divine or radiant damage it takes each round gains S d6 additional radiant damage. The Conviction expenditure can vent Dissonance once.

source.originalText: Final Miracle: Word of Binding: Enemies in a large AoE are silenced, snared, and take +25% divine damage for 3 turns.

cards.name: Balance Restoration
cards.rangeAndTarget: 15-foot-radius area centered at a point within 30 feet
cards.effect: Balance Restoration. Tags: priest, healing, radiant. Choose up to three living allies and three enemies in the area. Roll S d8 once. Each ally regains the roll + M HP. Each enemy makes a Wisdom save, taking the same S d8 roll as radiant damage on failure or half on success.

source.originalText: Balance Restoration: Channel divine energy that both heals allies and damages enemies in an area, maintaining cosmic balance.

cards.name: Divine Judgment
cards.effect: Divine Judgment. Tags: priest, judgment. The target makes a Wisdom save; success ends the attempt. On failure it is marked. The first time on each of its turns that it deals damage to another creature, it takes radiant damage equal to half that actual damage rounded down, minimum 1, maximum your Cleric level. It repeats the Wisdom save at the end of each turn, ending the mark on success.

source.originalText: Divine Judgment: Mark an enemy for judgment, causing them to take damage proportional to the harm they inflict.

cards.name: Ritual of Cleansing
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to three living allies within 30 feet; secondary enemies within 15 feet of you
cards.effect: Ritual of Cleansing. Tags: priest, rite, cleanse. Each ally may end one of Charmed, Frightened or Poisoned. For each distinct condition actually removed, choose one enemy within 15 feet; each chosen enemy makes a Wisdom save. On failure it becomes Frightened of you until the end of its next turn. One enemy can be chosen only once per use.

source.originalText: Ritual of Cleansing: Perform a ritual that removes multiple negative conditions from allies while potentially imposing them on enemies.

cards.name: Word of Power
cards.effect: Word of Power. Tags: priest, divine. Choose one mode. Mercy: one willing living creature regains S d8+M HP. Rebuke: one Undead or Fiend makes a Constitution save, taking (S+1)d8 radiant on failure or half on success; failure also removes its Reaction until the start of its next turn. Command: one other hostile creature makes a Wisdom save; failure knocks it Prone and removes its Reaction until the start of its next turn. No mode changes beliefs, loyalty or ideology.

source.originalText: Word of Power: Speak a divine word that has different effects based on the target's nature and actions.

cards.name: Cosmic Equilibrium
cards.effect: Cosmic Equilibrium. Tags: priest, zone, healing, radiant. Once per round, when a living ally in the zone receives healing beyond its missing HP, redirect up to S+M of that excess as radiant damage to one enemy in the zone. Separately, once per round when an enemy in the zone takes radiant damage from one of your Cleric features, one ally in the zone regains up to S+M HP, not exceeding half the actual radiant damage dealt. These two conversions cannot trigger each other.

source.originalText: Cosmic Equilibrium: Create a zone where healing and harm are balanced, converting excess damage to healing and vice versa.

cards.name: Sanguine Rite
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self and one ally within 30 feet
cards.frequency: At most once on each of your turns
cards.effect: Sanguine Rite. Tags: cultist, rite, healing. When one of your Rites deals damage to at least one enemy, choose one living ally within 30 feet. That ally regains HP equal to half the actual damage dealt to one chosen damaged enemy, rounded down, maximum S+M HP. This healing cannot trigger Sanguine Rite again.

source.originalText: Sanguine Rite:  Rites damage enemies and heal allies for a portion of the same amount.

cards.name: Blasphemous Tongue
cards.duration: Until the next Sacrament pulse or effect end
cards.effect: Blasphemous Tongue. Tags: cultist, sacrament, doomed. At each pulse of your Sacrament, each enemy affected by that pulse makes a Wisdom save. On failure it becomes Doomed until the next pulse. While Doomed, HP healing it receives is reduced by S+M, minimum 0, and each positive timed buff on it counts down one additional round at the end of its turn. Repeated failures refresh rather than stack.

source.originalText: Blasphemous Tongue: Sacraments inflict Doomed, reducing healing received and buff duration.

cards.name: Dark Conviction
cards.frequency: At most once on each of your turns
cards.effect: Dark Conviction. Tags: cultist, conviction. During a real encounter, when a hostile non-summoned creature that meaningfully threatened the party dies after taking damage from one of your Cleric features since the start of your current turn, gain 1 Conviction. Friendly creatures, summoned creatures, trivial staged creatures and repeated corpse destruction never qualify.

source.originalText: Dark Conviction: Killing an enemy grants 1 Conviction instantly.

cards.name: Zealot's Touch
cards.effect: Zealot's Touch. Tags: cultist, rite, necrotic. When starting a Rite whose printed pulse would restore HP over multiple turns, you may designate a hostile creature instead of a healing recipient. At each applicable pulse that enemy makes a Wisdom save. On failure it takes necrotic damage equal to the Rite's rolled healing dice; on success it takes half. Flat healing bonuses are not converted. The enemy receives no healing.

source.originalText: Zealot's Touch: Healing over time effects become life drain if cast on enemies.

cards.name: Rite of the Crimson Choir
cards.effect: Final Miracle — Rite of the Crimson Choir. Tags: cultist, finale, summon, rite. Summon four spectral fanatics. Each has AC 14, 10 HP, Speed 30 feet and cannot take Reactions. Spend one Bonus Action on your regular turn to command the Choir; this explicitly priced Finale permits up to four surviving fanatics to each move up to its Speed and make one melee spell-like attack using your Cleric technique attack bonus against an enemy within 5 feet; on hit it deals 1d6+S necrotic damage and you regain 1 HP, maximum 4 HP per round from the Choir. When a fanatic reaches 0 HP, when concentration ends or after the third round, it explodes; enemies within 5 feet make Dexterity saves, taking 1d6 necrotic on failure or half on success. Fanatics grant no XP, loot, corpse, resurrection target or Conviction. The Conviction expenditure can vent Dissonance once.

source.originalText: Final Miracle: Rite of the Crimson Choir: Summon 4 fanatics for 3 turns. Each heals you for 10% of their damage dealt and explodes in death.

cards.name: Blood Sacrifice
cards.cost: Lose S+M actual HP from yourself or one willing ally within 5 ft
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self or one willing ally within 5 feet
cards.duration: Empowerment lasts until end of your next regular turn
cards.effect: Blood Sacrifice. Tags: cultist, sacrifice, conviction. The chosen creature loses S+M actual HP; this loss cannot be reduced, redirected or transferred and cannot reduce it below 1 HP. The donor must have strictly more current HP than this cost before activation; otherwise it is illegal. You gain 1 Conviction. Your next damaging or healing Rite or Invocation before the end of your next regular turn adds 1d8 to one rolled damage or healing component. A creature must be willing unless the target is you.

source.originalText: Blood Sacrifice: Sacrifice a portion of your health or an ally's to generate Conviction and empower your next divine ability.

cards.name: Dark Sacrament
cards.cost: 3 Conviction + 5 RP to start; 1 RP maintenance
cards.effect: Dark Sacrament. Tags: cultist, sacrament, rite, sustained, zone. On start and each paid maintenance pulse, roll S d6 once. Up to three enemies in the zone make Constitution saves, taking that roll as necrotic damage on failure or half on success. If at least one enemy takes damage, up to three living allies in the zone each regain floor(roll/2)+M HP. Maximum 3 pulses. The Conviction expenditure can vent Dissonance once.

source.originalText: Dark Sacrament: Perform a twisted ritual that drains life from enemies to heal allies or create other beneficial effects.

cards.name: Corrupt Divinity
cards.effect: Corrupt Divinity. Tags: cultist, debuff, control. The target makes a Wisdom save. On failure it takes -1 on attack rolls and saving throws. It repeats the save at the end of each turn, ending the effect on success. If a non-player NPC at or below one-quarter maximum HP fails the initial save by 10 or more, it is also Charmed by you until the end of its next turn. This never permanently converts allegiance, changes beliefs or overrides a player character's agency.

source.originalText: Corrupt Divinity: Channel corrupted divine energy to weaken enemies and potentially convert them to your cause.

cards.name: Zealot's Fervor
cards.effect: Zealot's Fervor. Tags: cultist, stance. For 3 rounds, once on each of your turns add S to one damage roll from a Cleric feature and S to one HP-healing roll from a Cleric feature. While the Fervor lasts, your AC is reduced by 1. The Conviction expenditure is not a Rite or Invocation and therefore does not vent Dissonance by itself.

source.originalText: Zealot's Fervor: Enter a state of religious frenzy, increasing your damage output and healing power at the cost of defense.

cards.name: Ritual of Undeath
cards.rangeAndTarget: One eligible corpse within 30 feet or one living ally within 30 feet
cards.effect: Ritual of Undeath. Tags: cultist, undead, rite. Choose one mode. Corpse Servant: one humanoid corpse dead no more than 1 minute rises for 3 rounds as a temporary thrall with AC 13, 10 HP, Speed 30 feet and one attack only when you spend your shared companion Bonus Action command using your Cleric technique attack bonus; on hit it deals S d6 necrotic. The thrall disappears at 0 HP or when duration ends and grants no XP, loot, new corpse, Conviction or resurrection target. Death Ward: one living ally is marked for 1 minute; the first time it would die during that duration, it instead remains at 1 HP and counts as both humanoid and undead until the end of its next turn. Neither mode removes Wounds. The Conviction expenditure can vent Dissonance once.

source.originalText: Ritual of Undeath: Perform a forbidden ritual that can temporarily raise fallen enemies as servants or prevent allies from dying by transforming them into undead-like entities.

completeEnvelope.authoringNotes: Provisional; editorial review applied; human table balance testing required

completeEnvelope.protectedInterfaceOriginal: Once per turn, spend 1 Blood Gauge while casting to prevent 1 Dissonance; the Agent routes Weave strain through blood rather than gaining free casts.
completeEnvelope.rpAuthority: Explicit fallback: Cleric CoreV2 curve ×0.5, halves upward
engine: Blood Gauge (BG) starts and ends each encounter at 0, capacity 3; Spill Control raises capacity 6 while known. Once on your own regular turn, a weapon attack that damages a hostile living creature grants 1 BG. Hemorrhage Slash uses this same trigger, not an additional one. Explicit critical/kill/refund features can add more, but total BG gained is capped 2 per round. Self-inflicted damage, allies, summons, helpless captives and repeated damage to a corpse never generate BG. Blood is an encounter resource, not a currency carried into rest.

Dexterity governs weapon attacks; Intelligence governs hemomancy save DC and M. S scales from Crimson Agent class level. A weapon technique includes only its printed attacks, with normal weapon die plus Dexterity (or Strength when that weapon requires it). No free attack is implied by attack-speed wording. Class BG and RP are separate. Once per turn when casting an ordinary spell, optionally spend 1 BG to prevent 1 of that cast's Dissonance gain, minimum 0; never reduce RP this way.

Your Bleed is a physical ongoing effect on a living, non-bloodless creature: 1d4 damage at the start of each of its next 3 turns, then ends. It is not a new attack and generates no BG or procs. Refresh duration instead of stacking; Blood Echo expressly allows two independent instances, maximum. An Action by the victim or an adjacent creature using a healer's kit ends all your Bleeds on that victim. Apply physical resistance/immunity normally. Track remaining ticks and creator per instance. Allied healing versions from Bloodweaver cost RP and never count as hostile Bleeds for detonation, spreading or generation.

One Blood Mark at a time on a living target with your Bleed, except Phantom Strike, which explicitly may apply the mark without Bleed. It does not add a free Bleed. Marks last 5 of your regular turns, expire on encounter end or if the target dies, and never create damage by themselves. Rupture requires the target still within 60 ft and line of effect; it spends the mark. A mark does not defeat cover, planar boundaries or bloodlessness. Bloodtrail has its own tracking limits.

Veinweaves are self buffs unless their card expressly allows an ally. They require concentration and one may be active. Crimson Harmony is an explicit exception permitting two Veinweaves as one linked concentration burden; a failed concentration check ends both. A non-Veinweave concentration effect replaces the whole group. BG is spent on activation; no upkeep unless printed. Damage-sharing is redirection before mitigation, not extra damage: apply each recipient's own defenses once and never redirect the redirected portion again.

The healing, execution and denial text below deliberately bounds the source's vague percentage/instant-kill claims. HP sacrificed is direct loss, bypasses temporary HP and defenses, cannot be redirected, and cannot reduce the donor below 1. Only a willing ally can donate. HP sacrifice is never damage for class triggers. No class feature here restores the dead or removes Wounds.

At level 1 learn the core Blood Gauge/Bleed rules automatically. Blood Mark and Veinweaver's Core remain selections; Quickblood can be selected and used without a second unlock tax. Veinweaver's Core improves that foundation as printed. Standard scheduled acquisition applies. Bloodbound Edge is automatic 9. At 10 choose Bloodweaver, Shadow Operative or Thirstborn; its Final Cut is automatic 20. Duplicate Hemostasis names are separate Arch and Bloodweaver IDs.

Capacity clarification: Blood Gauge automatically reaches capacity 6 at class 9. Spill Control allows reaching 6 early but never raises the cap above 6. This new explicit gate ensures a later 5-BG Final Cut can be used without an optional capacity selection. Gain cap 2/round and encounter reset 0 still apply.
workedExample: Bard-style example becomes Agent 5: DEX 16, INT 14, S 2, M 2, BG 0/cap 3, full class RP. Select Hemorrhage Slash, Quickblood, Blood Mark, Shroud at 1; Blood Tithe and Vital Targeting at 2; Rupture and Spill Control at 3. Capacity is now 6.
Turn 1: Hemorrhage Slash hits for ordinary weapon damage+2d6, applies Bleed, and gains 1 BG (not 2). Bonus Action Blood Mark pays 1 BG: balance 0. Target takes its first 1d4 Bleed on its next turn.
Turn 2: ordinary weapon attack hits and gains 1 BG. Keep the mark and save resources; Bleed ticks independently and grants no BG.
Turn 3: a second weapon hit gains 1 BG: balance 2. Bonus Action Quickblood spends 1 BG: balance 1. It gives movement, not another attack.

Turn 4: Rupture is an Action, pays 1 BG: balance 0 and consumes the mark. Target fails CON: takes(S+1)d8=3d8. Rupture is not a weapon hit, so it generates no replacement BG. Any remaining Bleed continues.
After the encounter BG becomes 0. Blood Tithe's used short-rest charge and spent RP do not refresh without an actual rest.
balanceQuestions: Does early setup take too many turns for one mark?
Can Bloodweaver protect without sacrifice loops or infinite healing?
Are denial and execution limits sufficient against bosses and multiclass dips?

cards.name: Arterial Cut
cards.effect: A critical weapon hit applies your Bleed. If it already has your Bleed, extend one instance by 2 ticks, maximum 5 ticks remaining. This damage never generates further BG.

source.originalText: Arterial Cut: Critical hits apply Bleed for 3 turns; Bleed duration +2 turns.

cards.name: Blood Tithe
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self after a hostile bleeding creature dies within 30 ft
cards.effect: Regain HP equal to M+class level after a creature bearing your Bleed dies. It must have been an active hostile combatant; no ally, summon, captive or corpse farming.

source.originalText: Blood Tithe: Killing a bleeding target restores 10% of max HP.

cards.name: Veinweaver's Core
cards.effect: You can dismiss a Veinweave without an action and switch to another known Veinweave using its normal activation. Once/short rest reduce the BG cost of one Veinweave by 1, minimum 1. The basic one-Veinweave capacity is part of your engine, not locked behind this selection.

source.originalText: Veinweaver's Core: Unlocks use of Veinweaves (1 active at a time).

cards.name: Vital Targeting
cards.effect: Add S damage to a weapon hit against a target that has not perceived you or is within 5 ft of another conscious hostile-to-it ally. This is flat damage, not a critical die, and requires an actual weapon hit.

source.originalText: Vital Targeting: +15% damage to flanked or unaware enemies.

cards.name: Shroudstep
cards.effect: After taking the Hide Action and moving at least 10 ft while hidden, gain+1 AC. You still need valid concealment and a successful ordinary Stealth check; this feature does not grant invisibility.

source.originalText: Shroudstep: After using stealth movement, gain +10% dodge for 1 turn.

cards.name: Hemorrhage Slash
cards.effect: Make one weapon attack. On hit add S d6 damage of the weapon type and apply Bleed. The usual once/turn hit trigger grants 1 BG; this card grants no separate BG.

source.originalText: Hemorrhage Slash: A precise strike that deals moderate damage and applies Bleed status to the target, generating 1 Blood Gauge point.

cards.name: Veinweave: Quickblood
cards.effect: Start a Veinweave: gain+10 ft Speed and ignore nonmagical difficult terrain. Once during its duration you may draw or stow one weapon without using your object interaction. It grants no attacks or Actions.

source.originalText: Veinweave: Quickblood: Consume 1 Blood Gauge point to increase your movement and attack speed by 15% for 3 turns.

cards.name: Blood Mark
cards.rangeAndTarget: One living target with your Bleed within 60 ft
cards.effect: Apply your Blood Mark. Replaces your previous mark without detonating it. The mark enables Rupture and printed mark interactions; it deals no automatic damage and does not grant vision.

source.originalText: Blood Mark: Apply a magical mark to a bleeding target that lasts for 5 turns. The mark can be detonated for additional effects.

cards.name: Shroud
cards.duration: Until end next turn or attack/cast/bright light
cards.effect: Become invisible while in dim light or darkness. Attacking, casting a spell or entering bright light ends it. You must still Hide to conceal your location. Audible movement can reveal your position.

source.originalText: Shroud: Enter stealth mode, becoming invisible to enemies until you attack or move into bright light. Limited uses per encounter.

cards.name: Vital Sense
cards.rangeAndTarget: Living creatures within 60 ft, excluding total cover
cards.effect: Sense presence and approximate direction, not identity or thoughts. Once during this minute, gain advantage on one weapon attack against a sensed creature you can otherwise legally target. This does not change critical range.

source.originalText: Vital Sense: Heighten your senses for 1 minute, allowing you to detect the presence of living creatures within 60 feet and see their vital points more clearly (+10% critical hit chance).

cards.name: Blood Echo
cards.effect: Your Bleed can have two independent instances on a creature; a third application refreshes the oldest. Once on each of your turns add 1 to one Bleed instance's next tick. Never spread or detonate more instances than actually exist.

source.originalText: Blood Echo: Bleeds now stack twice and deal +10% more damage.

cards.name: Bio-Alchemical Flow
cards.effect: Activating a self-only Veinweave does not itself end your hidden state or Shroud. Its normal visible effects may reveal you; attacks, spells and other hostile effects still break hiding normally.

source.originalText: Bio-Alchemical Flow: Veinweaves do not break stealth.

cards.name: Spill Control
cards.effect: Blood Gauge capacity rises from 3 to 6. Gain rate is unchanged. This replaces, rather than adds to, the old cap. No BG is granted merely by learning it.

source.originalText: Spill Control: Max Blood Gauge increased to 6.

cards.name: Rupture Trigger
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to 2 other enemies within 5 ft of ruptured mark
cards.effect: After Rupture damages its marked target, choose up to 2 other living enemies nearby. Each makes CON save; on failure apply one Bleed. These applications do not trigger Rupture again or grant BG.

source.originalText: Rupture Trigger: Detonating a Blood Mark causes AoE Bleed in a small radius.

cards.name: Crimson Flow
cards.effect: After spending BG, gain+5 ft Speed. Your next weapon damage roll before end next turn adds 1. Repeated expenditures refresh rather than stack; no attack-speed or additional-Action benefit.

source.originalText: Crimson Flow: Using Blood Gauge grants +10% movement and attack speed for 2 turns.

cards.name: Crimson Harmony
cards.effect: You may sustain two Veinweaves as one concentration group. Both pay full costs and use normal activations; failing concentration ends both. Identical Veinweaves never stack, and no ordinary concentration spell can join this group.

source.originalText: Crimson Harmony: Maintain 2 Veinweaves simultaneously.

cards.name: Bloodbound Edge
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to 3 enemies with your Bleed within 30 ft
cards.effect: End up to 2 of your Bleed instances per target. Each takes 1d4 per remaining tick, maximum S d4 per creature, ignoring resistance but respecting immunity. This replaces their future ticks and grants no BG, healing or kill-trigger benefit.

source.originalText: Capstone – Bloodbound Edge: Once per rest, convert all Bleeds on enemies to instant True Damage.

cards.name: Veinweave: Bloodshield
cards.effect: Start Bloodshield Veinweave. Gain temporary HP equal to class level+M. Once while they remain, use Reaction to reduce damage to yourself by S. No self-damage refund or BG is generated.

source.originalText: Veinweave: Bloodshield: Consume 2 Blood Gauge points to create a protective barrier that absorbs damage equal to 20% of your maximum health.

cards.name: Rupture
cards.effect: Target makes CON save: (S+1)d8 necrotic on failure, half on success. The mark ends either way; existing Bleed remains. Damage from this technique is not a weapon hit and grants no BG.

source.originalText: Rupture: Detonate a Blood Mark on a target, dealing significant damage and consuming the mark.

cards.name: Bloodtrail
cards.rangeAndTarget: One living target with your Bleed within 30 ft
cards.effect: Know the direction to the target while within 1 mile on the same plane. Total distance and a trail are not shown. Lead barriers or effects that block divination block this sense; it grants no attack advantage or targeting through cover.

source.originalText: Bloodtrail: Mark a bleeding target, allowing you to track them perfectly for 1 hour regardless of distance or obstacles.

cards.name: Veinweave: Sensory Theft
cards.rangeAndTarget: One living creature with your Bleed within 60 ft
cards.effect: Target makes WIS save. Failure lets you see and hear through it while it remains within 1 mile on the same plane; you are blind/deaf to your own surroundings. It repeats save at the end of each of its turns and the first time each round it takes damage. No control or thought reading.

source.originalText: Veinweave: Sensory Theft: Consume 2 Blood Gauge points to briefly experience what a bleeding target sees and hears.

cards.name: Hemostasis
cards.effect: End all Bleed on the target and restore S d6+M HP, regardless of number of ticks removed. You cannot create extra healing by inflicting extra Bleed. Works even if no Bleed is present, at the same RP cost.

source.originalText: Hemostasis: Stop all bleeding effects on yourself or an ally, converting each remaining turn of Bleed into a small amount of healing.

cards.name: Bloodbond
cards.effect: Create Bloodbond while both remain within 30 ft. When ally takes damage, you may use Reaction to redirect floor(one-quarter of pre-mitigation damage) to yourself; each recipient applies its own defenses once. Once/round when a paid technique heals you, ally gains M temporary HP. No recursive transfers.

source.originalText: Bloodbond: Link with an ally; share 25% incoming damage and transfer 10% healing to them.

cards.name: Hemostasis
cards.rangeAndTarget: One willing living ally in range of your Bleed application
cards.effect: You may replace a new Bleed application on that ally with healing 1d4 at start of its next 3 turns. Pay extra RP even if original application was free. One such healing effect per target; it cannot spread, detonate, generate BG or trigger healing loops.

source.originalText: Hemostasis: Bleeds applied to allies now heal them instead.

cards.name: Protective Flow
cards.rangeAndTarget: Allies actually affected by your Veinweaves
cards.effect: An affected ally gains+1 to saves and reduces each damage instance by 2, minimum 0. This benefit does not stack across Veinweaves or Agents. Self-only Veinweaves cannot be extended merely by this passive.

source.originalText: Protective Flow: Allies affected by your Veinweaves gain 10% DR and +1 to all saves.

cards.name: Veinlock Tether
cards.rangeAndTarget: Willing linked ally within 30 ft being damaged
cards.effect: While your Bloodbond or Vitality Link is active, redirect up to S+M damage to yourself before mitigation. This is an alternative to Bloodbond's quarter-sharing reaction, not an additional redirection. Redirected damage cannot be redirected again.

source.originalText: Veinlock Tether: Form a damage-sharing link with an ally for 3 turns.

cards.name: Crimson Pact
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to 3 bleeding enemies and 6 living allies within 30 ft
cards.effect: End your Bleeds on chosen enemies; each makes CON save against 4d8 necrotic, half on success. Each chosen ally regains 4d8+M HP and gains 10 temporary HP. Use one shared roll per damage/healing effect; healing does not multiply by enemies or remaining ticks.

source.originalText: Final Cut – Crimson Pact: Detonate all enemy Bleeds to heal nearby allies and grant them barriers. (1/day)

cards.name: Transfusion
cards.cost: 2 RP; sacrifice up to class level HP
cards.effect: Lose K real HP, at least 1, without falling below 1. Ally regains K+floor(K/2) HP. Loss bypasses defenses and cannot trigger BG, damage-sharing or healing refunds. The RP/use limit remains even if little healing is possible.

source.originalText: Transfusion: Transfer health from yourself to an ally, healing them for 150% of the health sacrificed.

cards.name: Veinweave: Vitality Link
cards.effect: Start Vitality Link Veinweave. Once/round when you restore real HP with a paid Agent technique, linked ally regains M HP if within 30 ft. This secondary healing never triggers another link. Gain+1 AC while adjacent to that ally; no spell buffs or resources are copied.

source.originalText: Veinweave: Vitality Link: Consume 3 Blood Gauge points to link with an ally, sharing beneficial effects and healing for 3 turns.

cards.name: Blood Ward
cards.rangeAndTarget: Fixed 10 ft radius centered within 30 ft, up to 3 allies
cards.effect: Choose acid, cold, fire, lightning or necrotic. Selected allies within the zone gain resistance to that damage type. Leaving loses the benefit; reentering restores it. Identical resistance does not stack. This is not a Veinweave.

source.originalText: Blood Ward: Create a protective circle using blood magic that shields allies within from certain types of damage or effects.

cards.name: Purify Blood
cards.effect: End Poisoned and one nonmagical disease. Magical disease needs a successful INT ability check against its stated treatment DC, or DC 15 if absent; failure spends the cost. No curse, Wound, death or Corruption removal.

source.originalText: Purify Blood: Remove poison, disease, or other blood-borne afflictions from a target.

cards.name: Lifewell
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to 3 living allies within 15 ft
cards.effect: Spend K BG. At start and on each of your next 2 turns, use Bonus Action and pay 1 RP to pulse healing: each chosen ally still within 15 ft regains 1d8+K HP. Without maintenance it ends at turn end. Total 3 pulses; no triggers create more BG.

source.originalText: Lifewell: Ultimate ability that converts all your remaining Blood Gauge into a powerful healing aura for allies.

cards.name: Ghost Vein
cards.effect: A weapon hit made from hidden ignores resistance to that weapon's damage type for this hit. Immunity remains. This does not bypass armor or make the attack automatically hit.

source.originalText: Ghost Vein: Attacks from stealth ignore 25% of target resistances.

cards.name: Blackout Agent
cards.rangeAndTarget: Attacker within 30 ft that missed you
cards.effect: Attacker makes CON save; failure Blinded. Requires it can see you. Each creature becomes immune to your Blackout Agent until encounter end after resolving this save, preventing repeated blind-lock.

source.originalText: Blackout Agent: Dodging an attack blinds the attacker for 1 turn.

cards.name: Ghostflow Reflexes
cards.effect: Gain+1 AC. Once/round after a Veinweave starts, shorten one OTHER positive Agent cooldown by 1; this uses that ability's reset allowance. It grants no critical immunity, actions or per-rest uses.

source.originalText: Ghostflow Reflexes: While Veinweave is active: +5% dodge, cooldowns -1, +10% crit resistance.

cards.name: Veinjammer
cards.rangeAndTarget: One creature damaged by your Bleed
cards.effect: After a Bleed tick, choose that victim: Speed reduced 5 ft, minimum 0, and its next concentration save takes-1. Nonstacking; does not remove an Action or prohibit spellcasting.

source.originalText: Veinjammer: Bleeds reduce enemy casting and action speed by 10%.

cards.name: Total Silence
cards.effect: Each makes CON save. Failure prevents verbal spellcasting and Reactions, and suppresses one passive bonus to AC or attack rolls chosen from an observed effect. It never removes innate anatomy, immunities, legendary rules or class resource pools. Success prevents all effects; no whole-sheet passive disable.

source.originalText: Final Cut – Total Silence: AoE disables all enemy passives and silences for 2 turns.

cards.name: Phantom Strike
cards.rangeAndTarget: One enemy in weapon reach; must be hidden from it
cards.effect: Make one weapon attack with advantage. On hit add S d6 damage and apply a mark without its usual BG cost, even if not already bleeding. The mark replaces your old mark; no free Rupture occurs. Normal hit BG gain still capped.

source.originalText: Phantom Strike: Attack from stealth with increased critical chance and apply a Blood Mark automatically.

cards.name: Veinweave: Shadow Meld
cards.effect: Start Shadow Meld Veinweave: advantage on Stealth and invisible while motionless in dim light/darkness. Moving removes invisibility until start next turn; attacking or casting ends the Veinweave. No concealment against blindsight or effects that expressly reveal invisibility.

source.originalText: Veinweave: Shadow Meld: Consume 3 Blood Gauge points to become nearly undetectable for 1 minute, gaining enhanced stealth capabilities.

cards.name: Disrupt Flow
cards.effect: CON save: failure prevents Reactions and gives disadvantage on its next spell attack. If concentrating, make an additional normal concentration save versus your class DC. This never disables all special abilities or guarantees a failed concentration check.

source.originalText: Disrupt Flow: Temporarily disable a target's special abilities by disrupting their vital energies.

cards.name: Blood Cipher
cards.rangeAndTarget: One willing or restrained living target with your Bleed touched
cards.effect: Target makes WIS save unless willing. On failure learn one factual sensory memory from the last 24 hours about a stated event; the target chooses a relevant memory if several exist. Success yields no information. No beliefs, absolute truth or unrelated secrets are guaranteed.

source.originalText: Blood Cipher: Extract information directly from a bleeding target's blood, potentially learning secrets or weaknesses.

cards.name: Blackout
cards.effect: Create magical darkness blocking ordinary sight and darkvision. You can see within it up to 30 ft. Creatures can leave normally; no automatic damage, surprise or advantage when another sense locates you. Enemies still act and make saves normally.

source.originalText: Blackout: Ultimate ability that creates a zone of magical darkness where only you can see clearly, granting significant advantages.

cards.name: Blood Frenzy
cards.effect: Add 1 to direct weapon damage per hostile creature bearing your Bleed, maximum 3. Applies once per hit, not per Bleed instance. Secondary Bleed, copies and explosions gain no bonus.

source.originalText: Blood Frenzy: +5% damage per enemy actively bleeding (max +25%).

cards.name: Hemorrhagic Plague
cards.rangeAndTarget: One new living enemy within 5 ft of a Bleed victim
cards.effect: After one of your Bleeds ticks, pay 1 BG; new target makes CON save. Failure applies one Bleed. A spread instance cannot spread again. This grants no BG and does not duplicate marks or immediate damage.

source.originalText: Hemorrhagic Plague: Bleeds automatically spread to nearby enemies every 3 turns.

cards.name: Pain-to-Power Conduction
cards.rangeAndTarget: One enemy within 5 ft after it damages you
cards.effect: End one active Veinweave. Chosen enemy makes CON save: failure takes S d4 necrotic and Bleed; success takes half immediate damage only. On failure by 10 it is Frightened until end next turn. No resource refund.

source.originalText: Pain-to-Power Conduction: Veinweaves explode when struck, dealing AoE Bleed and minor Fear.

cards.name: Carrion Conductor
cards.rangeAndTarget: One fresh hostile living-combatant corpse within 30 ft
cards.effect: Mark the corpse once; on activation or before expiry use Reaction to burst it. Up to 3 enemies within 5 ft make DEX saves: S d6 necrotic, half on success. Corpse cannot be reused, raised by this effect or provide BG/kill triggers.

source.originalText: Carrion Conductor: Corpses leave behind blood pools that explode for AoE damage.

cards.name: Veinburst Requiem
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to 6 enemies with your Bleed within 30 ft
