operational.provenance: Printed cost multiplier×4 retained; all body sizing/weight rules below explicitly NEW beside null sourceWeight. Bind one actual reviewed ordinary armor model, not an undefined armor bonus.
operational.priceRule: 4× the selected Standard ordinary armor baseline price; this exact barding rule replaces, not multiplies again by, the general Large price multiplier. A genuine separately sourced grade/fit contract must identify its own rule, never be inferred.
operational.massRule: NEW actual selected baseline armor mass×2 Medium,×4 Large,×8 Huge. Smaller sizes need their own actual fitted model, not a placeholder. The source weight remains null.
operational.maximumHPRule: reviewed base armorHP×1 Medium,×2 Large,×4 Huge (Huge NEW); actual existing workmanship/grade rules apply once
operational.armorRule: actual selected armor AC formula, Dex cap, STR requirement, Stealth penalty and other printed properties; choose among eligible AC formulas under equipment rules, never add its AC to naturalAC
operational.wearerTraining: TR-07 animal armor-category habituation grants only ordinary fitted wearing competence for that category; not a humanoid/class proficiency or new armor source
operational.equipping: actual armor don/doff time from that reviewed model, with one capable helper occupied; no instant barding or resized armor on transformation
operational.capacity: actual mass counts on mount; no cargo space or extra carry rating
operational.repair: actual sized barding-body value and generic armor rule; not the whole animal price/HP
operational.primaryConstituents: actual armor main body and creation history, not an invented virtual rating

profiles.name: Carriage
profiles.operationalStatus: NEW SOURCE-AUTHORING PROFILE; exact candidate not yet approved

sourceNumericBindings.priceCp: sourcePriceCp retained; null for variable barding
sourceNumericBindings.mountSpeedAndCarry: exact sourceFields for nine mounts only; other numeric profiles are NEW

operational.provenance: Price retained; Cart maximumHP30 binds the reviewed ordinary cart body. Every other listed body quantity/geometry/handling number is NEW. No passengers, animals, harnesses, operators or contents are included in price.
operational.speedRule: minimum current fitted puller Speed and cap. Each actual puller draw rating, combined gross vehicle+payload draw limit, route fit, stability and terrain must pass. One named Burdened penalty applies when either carried or gross-draw threshold qualifies; no duplicate penalty for the same mount.
operational.terrain: firm wheel-supporting route; no ordinary climbing, stairs, ladders, swimming or unsupported gaps
operational.operatingFootprint: vehicle envelope plus actual puller footprint and at least5ft forward harness gap; route must contain all real widths/heights/turning space
operational.turning: one90-degree turn needs traveled distance at least the vehicle length and a clear swept envelope; sharper/blocked maneuver needs an actual separate route/work plan, not an automatic check
operational.controls: driver uses one Action per regular turn in tactical operation to guide/brake using the actual reins/lever and one hand; NEW manual brakes are included. Pullers expend actual movement in the linked drive event. Driver cannot claim a separate mounted turn for a pulling animal or duplicate movement by changing drivers. Outside initiative driving is continuous actual work, not rest.
operational.movementEvent: one linked vehicle/puller movement event per numbered round; resolve after required current driver Action and puller movement budgets are available. No future crew Action is presumed. All contributing budgets spent once. No vehicle Dash/Disengage/Reaction/attack; actual pullers have only their legal creature Actions.
operational.loadingRule: TR-12, real necessary handling; setup harness is additional, no free load/receivers

operational.provenance: Price retained; EVERY mass,HP,geometry,draft,crew,seat,cargo,propulsion and Speed number is explicitly NEW provisional game-profile authorship. No outside vessel stat block, inherent weapons, crew or cargo imported.
operational.inventoryIncluded: actual hull, principal mast/sail/rigging where sail mode exists, oars/rowlocks for stated oar mode, ordinary rudder/tiller and mooring lines. No crew, food/water, personal gear, cargo, weapons, lifeboat, magic or elemental power.
operational.crewGate: one designated trained Vehicles(Water) helmsman for hazardous navigation; actual capable crew meet each mode minimum and work continuously. Calm ordinary paddling/rowing may be physically attempted untrained without automatic penalty; uncertainty uses TR-09 actual check. Source-specific proficiency gates override.
operational.movementEvent: one vessel drive event per numbered round after a current helm Action and all required actual crew contributions for that mode are available. One person may satisfy rowboat helm+oar in one combined Action, otherwise each required crew member is distinct. Resolve after the last necessary contributing turn/Action, rechecking current feasibility. Contributions cannot also make attacks/Help/guard/beneficial rest. Extra Actions/extra turns or a new helm do not make a second event. No native vessel turn,Reaction,Dash,Disengage or attack.
operational.travel: actual continuous staffed labor on FL-03 clock; speed is one active hour basis, not miles per second. Crew shifts need real people, food and rest. Passengers can perform compatible limited activity only if real movement/environment permits; no automatic rest or full workshop.
operational.currentWind: actual route must supply water-current vector and sail feasibility. No stated current defaults to0 in the synthetic model only, not proof of calm seas. Sail calm or directly unsupported wind course gives0 self-propulsion; oars can still work if supplied. Ordinary usable wind gives stated sail speed; declared adverse-but-usable conditions halve it. Stronger weather needs actual hazard stakes, not an automatic new storm. Tactical actual current displacement is separate from own propulsion; countercurrent subtracts along route, minimum0 ground progress, with actual drift retained.
operational.turning: clear swept envelope required; a90-degree heading change requires at least one hull-length traveled and sufficient water/clearance, or an actual stationary line/anchor maneuver taking10 active minutes with working crew. No instant spin through walls.
operational.docking: actual slow approach, available berth/bank, water depth, lines and capable receiver/crew. Uncontested calm docking needs no roll; hazardous approach uses declared Vehicles(Water) DC and failure under TR-09. Load/unload is extra real handling. Mast lowering is not free; separate actually feasible20-minute crew operation, mast/clearance accounted during it.
operational.primaryConstituents: original principal keel/hull frame and steering body; original primary mast/rig where needed to restore that same sail assembly. Compatible planking, cloth sails, ropes, oars and subordinate fittings may be replaced with actual stock, not invented from a cost quotation.
operational.zeroHP: Broken and propulsion disabled. If afloat and no specific different destruction source governs, NEW begins one10-minute flooding/evacuation deadline; at it the wreck becomes submerged/stranded according to actual depth/bank/support, not deleted. Occupants receive actual fall/swim/drowning/escape procedures, not automatic death or shared hull damage. Repairing, touching or renaming the hull cannot reset that event.
operational.emergencyShoring: NEW once per actual hull-breaking damage episode: two capable workers, at least one trained Carpenter tools or Vehicles(Water), real compatible patch/bracing material priced at1%undamaged body reference (minimum1gp),five uninterrupted active minutes before the flooding deadline; DC15 appropriate tool task,Core collapsed binary. Success keeps that same disabled hull afloat for60 minutes from completion, withoutHP,propulsion or a new seaworthy status; failure spends work/materials and does not alter deadline. It cannot be repeated on that same rupture to bank time. Grounding/towing to genuine support may permit later full repair.
operational.repair: TR-14 actual structural repair, full required original body, trained suitable toolkit, dry/supportable worksite; generic25%body material reference/DC10/max(1h,maxHP/10h) unless a specific actual repair authority differs. Core complete service quote10%/15% is an alternative, not another material charge. No repair while the purported workpiece is irretrievably absent.

completeTransportDirections.title: Nine real mount profiles

originalQuestion.title: Nine named mounts have partial profiles
originalQuestion.question: Keep all nine exact Player purchase prices, tactical speeds and pound-carry capacities. Complete actual size, body weight where needed, ability/AC/HP/save/action/sense/training profiles from real sources or explicitly NEW authoring. Do not reverse-engineer Strength or size from a capacity or import another game's stat block. The bounded Known Descent search found no exact mount-name paragraphs, including table paragraphs; that is not a claim about every archive.

completeTransportDirections.disposition: KEEP nine exact prices/Speed/carry fields; NEW complete animal templates
completeTransportDirections.authoringWording:
Adopt the nine separately keyed NEW provisional operational profiles in EX58_TRANSPORT_PROFILES.json: Camel; Donkey or mule; Elephant; Horse,draft; Horse,riding; Horse,war; Mastiff; Pony; Warhound. Each preserves its full original row, original null mass/status and exact printed price, walking Speed and pounds capacity. The body's new size/mass/abilities/AC/HP/Hit Dice/senses/attack/training/food/draw/Load fields are explicit game-authoring choices, not recovered monster statistics, real-world animal claims, or Strength reverse-engineered from carrying capacity. Donkey or mule identifies one chosen actual individual, not two animals.

Use the catalogue's fixed naturalAC (already including that body's Dexterity), fixed ordinary maximumHP, current actualHP and real Hit Dice. No class level, RP/RC, class feature, special immunity, darkvision or magical nature is supplied. Listed independent attacks are one Action/one attack using the actual attack bonus, reach, dice/modifier/type and normal Core attack criticals; they have no automatic knockdown, charge damage, Multiattack or mounted-rider attack grant. Saves use actual ability modifiers without new save PB; changes from Wounds/conditions are real. The NEW threat reference level is for FL-16 comparison only and is expressly not CR or class level. An effect requiring an actual source CR or other missing special predicate cannot substitute this reference number; it needs that particular predicate, not another broad transport conference.

Large templates occupy10ft squares, Medium5ft and NEW Huge15ft. The one saddle seat admits an actually compatible rider at least one size smaller. A Small rider on a Medium Pony/Mastiff/Warhound still must satisfy both physical weights and the new explicit Load cap; a Medium rider cannot ride them merely because a small weight fits. Each mount's source carry-pounds cap is a specific profile limit; its separately NEW Load cap is deliberately not recalculated from the independently authored STR. Carried saddle/gear/rider/containers/contents count, with one Burdened penalty where the actual threshold is reached. Draw capacity is its own explicit NEW harness-mode value, not more back-carry capacity.

NEW default registered Expedition mount is a significant actual creature using reviewed Core Wounds/dying/death saves. Actual registered significance is fixed before the encounter, not changed after a fatal result. A truly different source lifecycle wins: an actual bonded Ranger Beast uses its HP-only/immediate-death/no-Death-saves procedure, not this ordinary default, with original animal/remains history. No generic healing, repair, insurance, stabling payment or new template resurrects a dead individual. A healthy template describes an available type, not evidence that the merchant's actual specimen has fullHP, training, supplies or willingness.

completeTransportDirections.title: Riding control, training and actor caps

originalQuestion.title: Living mount control and agency
originalQuestion.question: The Player explicitly distinguishes trained controlled mounts from independent intelligent or untrained mounts. Decide how actual training, willingness and compatible anatomy establish that relation, including rider incapacity and loss of contact. The controlled Action list is Dash, Disengage, Dodge; do not silently add an attack or impose crafted-automaton binding. State any shared actor/command budgets by actual governing source. An independent creature keeps its actual agency, rather than becoming a free second player character.

completeTransportDirections.disposition: KEEP trained controlled versus independent; NEW finite training/command bridge
completeTransportDirections.authoringWording:
KEEP: a trained willing physically compatible mount may be controlled; an intelligent or untrained independent mount keeps its own agency. Independent is a behavioral/turn designation, not permission for a player to direct a third free combat character. A mount's sale, ownership, restraint or payment does not demonstrate willingness or training. An actual independent NPC who joins as a character counts in the12-character roster. A merely ridden animal is not another member seat, but its actor/action/food/cargo records remain real.

NEW riding command bridge: a conscious nonincapacitated seated rider with a usable trained audible or tactile/rein channel can direct the controlled mount's intended movement and choose its one allowed Action (Dash, Disengage or Dodge) for the linked regular-turn sequence. The actual short cue fits LAX's shared speech allowance, or the practiced reins/weight cue uses that existing trained channel; it is not a free universal language. Reins need one actually available hand; trained tactile seat/leg cues may be used only where that individual was trained for them and the current seat/movement permits. No separate Bonus Action is imposed for this ordinary riding direction. It does not issue a class companion/device command, spend/refund its allowance, enable a controlled attack or transfer the rider's class bonuses to the animal. Physical driving a carriage/ship has its own paid Actions under TR-08/09.

A controlled mount has its own regular creature turn under TR-03 and counts as one commanded independent-turn actor toward the Loop's existing limit of two controlled independent combat-capable subordinates per controller; the controller's own character is not one of those subordinates. Source-bound companions using an attached phase and no full turn retain their own shared BA/one-offensive-allowance rules and do not acquire a full turn from the mount label. Do not compress excess ordinary independent animals into a newly invented swarm: a genuine cohort stat block would be needed. Additional ordinary pack animals may be led noncombat at actual handling cost but gain no third controlled combat turn/attack; if independent, the Director resolves their genuine agency rather than taking player attack orders.

When an essential control predicate is lost before the mount acts (rider no longer seated, incapacitated, no usable cue, mount incapacitated/unwilling), its still-existing turn does not disappear or refresh. Without a valid current rider cue it defensively Dodges if able and stays still or moves only to an actually available immediately safer space, chosen by its real agency, not a free tactical attack order. A cue already executed is not undone; an issued but unexecuted ordinary riding cue is rechecked at execution and cannot compel an animal whose current control relation ended. This differs explicitly from the protected already-issued attached companion command, whose owner becoming incapacitated alone need not cancel it. A standing trained noncombat lead/follow cue outside danger may continue when its actual conditions and handler remain available; no unattended mount program or unlimited work follows.

NEW training completion: for a genuinely tame/willing ordinary specimen, basic riding or harness training is one40-active-hour course for that named function; each actual animal can credit at most four training hours/day, and trainer time counts as work. Instructor requires actual Animal Handling proficiency, suitable safe space, properly fitting tack and a usable conditioning method. Credit15-minute completed phases; interruption loses only unfinished phase credit, not actual time/feed/cost. The NEW full-course instruction reference is5gp, actual tuition/voluntary arrangements may differ; feed/water/tack/stabling are real separate provisions unless included in a documented offer. Completion is deterministic after the actual course and demonstrated safe routine behavior, not a magical obedience check; it grants only that practiced ordinary function. Previously genuinely documented training needs no retroactive course. 'Wild' or unwilling is not trained by depositing40 hours: acquiring/taming it requires its actual source/scene and genuine behavior first. War-named sale may include verified combat habituation in its actual contract; the name alone doesn't. These courses grant no attack/skill/class proficiency to the rider and no general Ranger bond authorization.

completeTransportDirections.title: One whole regular turn for a controlled mount

originalQuestion.title: Shared initiative and regular turn order
originalQuestion.question: Complete 'shares your initiative' with a precise controlled-mount phase, whole-turn order, movement splitting and regular start/end markers. Preserve existing effect clocks, Reaction refreshes, full-Action ceilings and spent movement. Mounting, dismounting, changing control or initiative, and extra rider turns cannot mint new mount turns or refresh existing resources. Decide mid-round entry and a mount whose regular turn already occurred.

completeTransportDirections.disposition: KEEP shared initiative; NEW order/entry accounting
completeTransportDirections.authoringWording:
NEW exact shared-initiative binding: at initiative registration, a controlled mount shares the rider's initiative value but takes one complete regular creature turn immediately AFTER that rider's complete regular turn. They do not interleave movement/Actions; the rider cannot ride20ft, pause the mount's turn to attack on an invented extra rider segment, then finish it. The rider can Ready an actually permitted Action, paying its Action and later Reaction, with its real trigger/duration/components; this does not grant a free mounted attack. An independent mount keeps its own initiative and actual choices.

The mount has its own current regular-start and regular-end markers, conditions, movement and one normal Action, subject to its controlled Dash/Disengage/Dodge list. It has an ordinary Reaction budget but, while controlled, no autonomous offensive Reaction or opportunity attack is supplied; a real specific defensive Reaction could operate only if its source permits. It rolls its own Core death saves when appropriate. Each regular start refreshes only its own allowed budgets and ticks its own counters. No rider extra turn creates another mount turn/start/recharge; no attached companion phase becomes a mount regular turn by renaming it.

NEW control/initiative transfer: each physical actor receives at most one scheduled regular turn per numbered round and keeps existing spent budgets/condition deadlines through mounting, dismounting or changing controllers. In-round changes do not move an already allocated or taken slot. A new valid controlled relation adopts the new rider's linked position beginning next numbered round; this round use the still-unspent original slot if any. A mount first admitted mid-round gets an eligible not-yet-passed insertion only under current combat entry rules, otherwise begins next round; never replay the new rider's passed slot. Dismounting to 'independent' does not obtain another turn. Record regularTurnId/round, original slot, prospective next slot, control history and spent move/Action/Reaction for that same animal.

At start/end apply the actual Core condition/death/ongoing/expiry order, not an added vehicle tick. A rider or mount effect expiring at a particular owner's marker follows that marker through the link; identical initiative does not merge the two creatures' clocks. Travel outside initiative accrues actual movement and work continuously without combat rewards/ticks duplicated at reentry. When multiple physical pullers drive one vehicle, TR-08's coordinated movement reservation is the specific NEW exception for its one linked vehicle event, not a general ability to split a ridden mount's turn.

completeTransportDirections.title: Mount, dismount and stay seated

originalQuestion.title: Mounting, dismounting and losing the seat
originalQuestion.question: Preserve half-Speed cost and the printed DC10 Dexterity save when a mount is moved against its will or knocked Prone. Complete reach, remaining movement, Speed0, fitting destination, frequency, prone rider, forced dismount and trigger identity. Distinguish the mount becoming Prone, actual falling and the rider becoming Prone; apply current Core saves and fixed falling procedures without inventing generic natural shifts or repeated saves for one event.

completeTransportDirections.disposition: KEEP half-Speed and DC10 DEX; NEW geometry/trigger completion
completeTransportDirections.authoringWording:
KEEP mounting or voluntarily dismounting costs half the rider's current walking Speed, rounded down in feet, from that rider's actually remaining regular movement budget. NEW: at most one mount OR dismount operation per regular turn; an extra turn does not grant another through this bridge. Rider Speed0, an unavailable required hand, incompatible body/seat, inaccessible destination or insufficient remaining movement prevents that ordinary operation; zero/odd Speed does not create a free mount. A positive Speed whose half rounds below1 costs1ft for this operation. This is ordinary movement cost, not a Bonus Action or the object's free interaction; specific independently operative features can override only their actual clause.

Begin within5ft of the actual accessible saddle/seat at a reachable height, with a stable legal approach, one usable supporting hand and an actual fitting destination. A high Elephant seat may need real steps/help or another legal movement route; an 'exotic saddle' does not lift the rider. A Prone rider first stands through its real movement cost, or needs actual assistance/another procedure; the mount operation alone does not remove Prone. The selected saddle cell/location and real supporting surface are recorded. Dismount to a visible actually free adjacent space within5ft of the relevant body boundary at a reachable level; cannot choose through a wall, onto another creature, inside an inadequate gap or across an unpaid fall. The mount retains its current movement/action/state, with no refill.

KEEP one DC10 Dexterity SAVE when the mount is actually moved against its will OR knocked Prone by one resolved source event while the rider is seated. It is a Core binary save: no natural1/20 shifts unless an actual specific rider grants them. The same event satisfying both descriptions triggers one save, not two. Several genuinely distinct events may each trigger their own save; current immunity/source restrictions apply. No save is created merely by voluntary ordinary mount travel, a harmless template rename, or by the rider's own Prone condition.

On a failed seat save the rider leaves the seat and lands Prone in the first legal adjacent space in its preregistered dismount preference or the Director's neutral accessible order. Resolve any actual height/fall under current falling rules; do not add an invented fixed damage packet just for unseating. On success retain the seat/control only if physical support remains possible. If the mount is Prone, a successful rider remains supported on the actual body but gains no immunity to its awkward seat, blocked movement or required later dismount; the rider does not automatically become Prone solely because the mount did. An impossible destination/support must be resolved as actual fall/entrapment, never occupancy of a wall. If the rider is independently made Prone, apply that condition without inventing a second DEX save; usable seat/control requires actual compatibility and TR-02. If a source physically ejects the rider irrespective of a save, use that source and the real landing instead of treating this ordinary seat save as a universal defense.

completeTransportDirections.title: Mounted geometry and opportunity attacks

originalQuestion.title: Opportunity attacks and mounted geometry
originalQuestion.question: The Player permits an opportunity attack provoked by a mount to target rider or mount. Reconcile actual sight, reach, line, legal targeting, Disengage, forced movement, teleport and one Reaction before attack resolution. Define rider position/footprint and area targeting without treating rider and mount as one creature, unlimited cover or a free extra attack.

completeTransportDirections.disposition: KEEP printed rider-or-mount target choice; NEW bounded seat footprint
completeTransportDirections.authoringWording:
NEW ordinary mounted geometry: the mount occupies its own declared space. Record one saddle/seat point or fitting5ft subspace on that physical body before movement; a rider's attacks, interaction reach, line and area exposure originate from its actual seat, not every edge of an Elephant's15ft footprint. Shifting to a different accessible position on the mount requires the rider's actual movement/path/support; it is not a free change of targeting origin. They remain two creatures with separate AC/HP/conditions/attunements/resources. An area can affect both if it actually includes each; roll separate saves and apply separate damage histories. Neither gains automatic cover, a sharedHP shield or a new immunity by riding. Ordinary actual cover from a barrier/body is adjudicated from its real geometry, never presumed whole-mount cover.

KEEP the Player's specific exception: when the mount's own actual voluntary movement provokes a legal opportunity attack, the reactor may select mount OR rider as the target. There must be actual visibility and a legal reach/line to that chosen target at the departure edge. Spend the reactor's one available Reaction and make one ordinary permitted attack before completing that departure step. The choice is not one attack on each, and selecting the rider does not extend a weapon's reach to an unreachable seat. One source movement provoking both labels is one opportunity, not two. The target uses its own actual AC/defenses and any genuinely legal defensive reaction; an attack against the mount does not automatically hit the rider or unseat them unless its actual consequence moves/prones the mount or another effect says so.

The mount's valid Disengage protects against opportunity attacks provoked by its movement and therefore removes this mounted target-choice opportunity for that move. The rider's own Disengage protects the rider's own voluntary movement; it does not give the mount Disengage or erase its provocation. Rider-only movement around/dismounting from the seat uses the rider's actual OA predicates. # Core resolution and injury playtest rules

This is the active provisional integration for rolls, damage, zero HP, Wounds and injuries in the developing campaign candidate. It resolves specific conflicts between approved Core V2, compatible Player Rulebook V6 rules and the retained Gameplay Loop. Original books and alternate procedures remain unchanged. Full conditions, equipment, hazards and recovery integration remain separate work.

Use with [class rules](CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md), [spell rules](SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md) and the [complete coverage ledger](GAME_DEVELOPMENT_COVERAGE.md). The [source conference](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/CODEX_CORE_RESOLUTION_CONFERENCE.json), [V6 findings](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/CODEX_CORE_SOURCE_FOLLOWUP.md) and [GPT proposal](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CORE_STATE_AND_INJURY_PROPOSAL.md) preserve the reasoning.

## Which rule applies

The domain authority is [Core Systems Known Descent V2](../../../../books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx). The approved [Player Rulebook V6](../../../../books/player/Decennium_Descent_Player_Rulebook_v6.docx) supplies compatible rules that Core does not replace. This overlay states the selected interpretation or newly authored rule wherever those sources leave a gap. An explicit exception on an operative, reviewed class/spell/item card applies only within its printed scope; a historical alternate or a same-named feature is not an extra grant. This candidate does not promote an entire historical branch.

| Question | Active rule and provenance | Inactive alternate |
|---|---|---|
| Attacks | Core V2: meet AC; natural 1 misses; natural 20 hits and doubles damage dice. | Applying the general Gameplay four-degree roll to attacks. |
| Task checks | Explicitly adopted Gameplay four degrees and natural shifts. | Assuming every critical result creates an unprinted effect. |
| Ordinary saves | Binary meet-DC test; printed failure margins remain literal. Natural 1/20 do not generically shift saves in this candidate. This separation is an integration choice. | Automatic critical saves or natural-result shifts inferred from the task rule. |
| Death-save timing | Core and V6: start of turn; regular-turn-only timing is a provisional guard. | Gameplay end-of-turn saves. |
| Wounds | Core trigger/save, Constitution-save and Hit-Dice-recovery penalties, and three-Wound Critical state. | Gameplay automatic Wound triggers, Hit Dice healing penalty, half Speed and Strain lock. |
| Named Wounded condition | Core paragraph 782 expressly describes the same Wound count, Constitution penalty, Hit Dice recovery and three-Wound Critical state. Apply those records once. | V6 Appendix A paragraphs 9971–9974 give a conflicting temporary condition cleared by magic/rest with Constitution-save disadvantage; Core replaces it here. |
| Stable, instant death, knockout and temporary HP | Compatible recovered V6 rules. | Treating these recovered rules as newly invented. |
| Ordinary Wound treatment | Explicit Gameplay-derived integration below. | Claiming it is original Core wording or ordinary HP healing. |
| Injury table and unresolved thresholds | New provisional choices below, with their search limits stated. | Dropping Core's failure-by-5 consequence because its table was not located. |

## Rolls

Choose the roll type before rolling. Use the actual ability modifier, including negative values, and normal proficiency only when applicable. Existing advantage/disadvantage chooses the higher/lower of two d20s; multiple sources do not stack, and any advantage plus disadvantage cancels. Add other legal modifiers once. Fractions round down unless a rule specifies otherwise. One tile is 5 feet. Class L, S and effect M retain their definitions in the shared class rules.

**Attack:** roll d20 plus the appropriate attack modifier against AC. Meeting AC hits. Natural 1 always misses; natural 20 always hits and critically doubles damage dice, not flat modifiers. Beating AC by 10 is not a critical hit. An explicit broader critical range does not stack with another; use the broadest eligible range. In this overlay, a natural result below 20 in that range must still meet AC unless the feature expressly says it always hits.

**Task, skill or tool check against a fixed DC:** total at least DC+10 is Critical Success; at least DC is Success; at most DC-10 is Critical Failure; other totals below DC are Failure. Natural 20 then improves one degree and natural 1 worsens one, bounded at either end. A task printing only success/failure collapses the two upper degrees to success and two lower degrees to failure; no extra consequence is invented. A natural 20 can still fail an otherwise impossible check, and a natural 1 with sufficient modifiers can still succeed.

**Saving throw:** total at least DC succeeds; otherwise it fails. Natural 1 and 20 have no generic special outcome. A printed failure by 5 or 10 compares the final total with the DC; it does not add an unprinted critical-save system. Death saves are the specific exception below.

**Opposed check, new provisional tie rule:** compare final totals. Higher wins; an exact tie leaves the existing state unchanged, so the initiating creature fails to change it. Do not turn task natural shifts into hidden numeric modifiers. A maneuver explicitly printing degree outcomes must specify how those apply.

## Resolve a damage event

Resolve each genuinely separate hit or damage event once. Do not split one packet to multiply Wound saves or combine separate hits merely to cross a threshold. Feature-specific prevention that acts before damage or before reaching zero resolves at its printed timing first.

1. Resolve attack/save, damage and applicable defenses. The remaining nonnegative amount is **resolved damage**.
2. Record HP, Wounds and zero-HP state before the event. Remove temporary HP first. **Post-temp damage = resolved damage minus temporary HP absorbed.** Keep this amount even when it exceeds current HP; floor the resulting current HP at zero.
3. Check V6 Instant Death. If post-temp damage minus HP before the hit is at least maximum HP, the creature dies. For a creature already at zero, this is post-temp damage at least maximum HP. Stop: there is no Wound save, death-save failure or successful knockout from that event.
4. Otherwise, a living creature makes one Wound save if it dropped from positive HP to zero, if **2 × post-temp damage is at least maximum HP**, or if the effect actually inflicts Maiming. Overlapping triggers still cause only one save. The post-temp threshold and one-save rule are new provisional interpretations. Maiming is an independent trigger even when temporary HP absorbs all ordinary damage; immunity to Maiming itself still applies.
5. Make a Constitution save against **max(10, floor(post-temp damage / 2))**. Use pre-event Wounds for the -1-per-Wound penalty. Maiming with zero post-temp damage uses DC 10. A Wound gained now cannot penalize the roll that created it.
6. A success adds no Wound. A failure that began with zero, one or two Wounds adds exactly one; failure by 5 or more also gives that Wound one Injury. A failure that began with three Wounds kills the creature instead: no fourth Wound and no Injury roll. Stop processing later living-target consequences if dead.
7. If the creature was already at zero before this event and post-temp damage is positive, end Stable. A creature using death saves adds one failure, or two for a critical hit; three failures kill it. An ordinary creature that does not use death saves dies instead, without starting death counters. A hit from positive HP to zero does not also cause a same-packet death failure.
8. If this event newly reduces positive HP to zero, a valid melee knockout makes the surviving creature Stable. Otherwise a character/significant NPC using death saves begins dying; an ordinary monster dies. A previously Stable creature whose temporary HP absorbed all damage remains Stable unless an independent Maiming result killed it. The Director identifies significant NPCs consistently. Knockout cannot override Instant Death or a fatal Wound save.

Core's Maiming and Wound trigger rules remain subject to an actual feature's eligibility. The reference helper receives already legal events; it does not grant every attack Maiming or a damage-prevention exception.

## Zero HP and recovery

A living character at zero HP is Unconscious. Core's condition already includes Incapacitated, unawareness, dropping held items and falling Prone; an adjacent hit is critical as specified there. Healing does not silently remove other independent causes of Unconscious or Prone.

While dying, make one death save at the **start of each regular initiative turn**. Roll d20 without modifiers unless a feature specifically modifies death saves. Natural 20 restores 1 HP; natural 1 adds two failures. Other results of 10 or more add one success; 9 or less add one failure. Three successes make the creature Stable; three failures make it Dead. Extra turns and Actions add no extra death saves. Stable or Dead creatures do not roll them.

Regaining positive HP or becoming Stable resets both counters. Temporary HP does not raise normal HP, end Unconscious or reset counters. Fully absorbed damage does not end Stable or add a death failure in this provisional interpretation. Independent Maiming can still cause its Wound save.

**Stabilize:** an Action and DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check, or an Action using one healer's-kit use automatically, stabilizes a living dying creature at zero. It remains Unconscious and makes no death saves. Roll 1d4 once when it becomes Stable and record its absolute recovery time that many hours later. If still Stable then, it regains 1 HP. Damage reaching normal HP cancels that deadline and resumes dying with the appropriate failures. Rest and Stable recovery use the same elapsed clock, so four hours of recovery inside an eight-hour Watch do not cost twelve hours. A later rest does not separately replay the Stable healing event.

**Dead:** ordinary healing and stabilization do not restore life. Resurrection must satisfy its own willing-soul, body, time, cost and target rules. It does not automatically remove Wounds, Corruption, debts, legal death or claims upon the body. Corpses cannot supply repeated resource triggers.

## Wounds and Critical state

Each Wound imposes **-1 Constitution saves** and reduces the normal maximum number of Hit Dice recovered per long rest by one, to a minimum of zero. It does not reduce each healing die. The broader recovery rules own the normal recovery maximum and rest legality.

At three Wounds the creature is **Critically Wounded**: Speed is reduced by 10 feet, to minimum zero, and the next failed Wound save is fatal. The failure that first raises two Wounds to three is not that later failure. Core's named **Wounded** condition (paragraph 782, preserved in [the 28-condition source register](../../data/playtest/core_condition_sources.json)) explicitly summarizes these same Wounds; it does not add duplicate penalties. Its conflicting V6 predecessor is inactive in this overlay. This individual source comparison does not complete the remaining condition audit.

**New provisional healing ceiling:** while Critical, healing cannot increase HP above **max(1, maximum HP - 1)**. Maximum HP itself does not change. Gaining the third Wound does not immediately remove existing HP; a later attempted heal also cannot reduce HP. The minimum of one permits recovery when maximum HP is one and is an explicit exception to “cannot regain full HP.” Removing enough Wounds to leave Critical removes its Speed penalty and ceiling, but does not itself heal HP.

## Linked injuries

The inspected eight approved books and current text sources reference an Injury table, but no actual table was located. The full Wound/Medicine searches of both Core editions found no alternate general treatment procedure. Those are search limits, not proof about every archive. This **new provisional d6 table** supplies Core's failure-by-5 consequence until a reviewed replacement is adopted.

| d6 | Injury | Exact penalty |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Concussion | -1 Initiative and Perception checks. |
| 2 | Offensive Trauma | -1 attack rolls. |
| 3 | Mobility Trauma | All non-teleport Speeds reduced by 5 feet, minimum zero. |
| 4 | Fine-Motor Trauma | -1 tool checks and Dexterity checks primarily manipulating an object, mechanism, lock or device. |
| 5 | Exertion Trauma | -1 Strength and Dexterity ability checks. |
| 6 | Cognitive Trauma | -1 Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma ability checks. |

Link each result to the one Wound just gained. An Injury never adds another Wound. Record duplicate results separately, but identical penalties apply once. Different Injury penalties affecting the same roll or stat also use only the strongest Injury penalty. V6 paragraph 7925 explicitly calls Initiative a Dexterity check, so both Concussion and Exertion Trauma can apply, with only one -1 Injury penalty. An injury affects future Initiative rolls, never an order already established. This does not change other Initiative procedures. Mobility Trauma can coexist with the separate Core Critical Speed penalty, applying both once. Other effects keep their own stacking rules.

Removing a Wound ends its linked Injury. A duplicate penalty persists while any remaining Wound carries that result. When a removal effect names no specific Wound, the patient chooses existing records. Injuries cause no extra damage, Actions lost, disadvantage, maximum-HP reduction or resource triggers. Describe equivalent trauma for unusual anatomy while retaining the printed penalty.

## Ordinary Wound treatment

This is an explicit Gameplay-derived integration. A living patient with at least one Wound receives eight elapsed hours of treatment with a medical kit and **one Supply**. **New provisional cost decision:** commit and consume that Supply once when treatment begins, on every attempt, even on success or interruption; no extra Supply is charged for failure. The retained Gameplay text requires one Supply and explicitly mentions consumption on failure but does not clearly settle success refunds. This candidate deliberately settles the ambiguity as a cost on every attempt, rather than claiming that interpretation is recovered source wording. Choose the Wound being treated before beginning. At completion roll Wisdom (Medicine) against the applicable tier DC: I 12, II 13, III 15, IV 16, V 18, VI 19. Unverified higher-tier procedures remain with the later Director/hazard pass.

Critical Success removes the chosen Wound and one other existing Wound chosen by the patient, if available. Success removes the chosen Wound. Failure removes none. Critical Failure removes none and gives the **patient** one Strain; identifying the patient is a new clarification. Associated Injuries end with removed Wounds. Treatment itself does not restore HP. Whether treatment qualifies as a legal rest is determined separately; the active healer cannot automatically claim an eight-hour Rest Watch while treating. Count the eight hours once, with any Stable recovery occurring on the same clock.

## Verification scope

`tools/core_playtest_rules.py` is a reference for roll types and the damage/Wound/death state transitions. It does not select legal Actions or targets, run all class reactions, roll damage, apply every defense, adjudicate all conditions, run medical-kit/Supply inventories or simulate a campaign clock. Its callers supply legal events and actual elapsed time. `tools/validate_core_playtests.py` reports named regression cases and sampled state invariants. Passing checks do not establish human balance or completion of the remaining game systems.

## Encounter and action resources

Establish terrain, light, hazards, objectives, exits and cargo; determine awareness; roll `d20 + DEX modifier + legal bonuses`. Highest first. Players choose player/player ties; the Director resolves ties involving NPCs. Keep the resulting ordered slots for the encounter. A round represents approximately six seconds. A **regular turn** is a creature's normal initiative slot even if it cannot act. An extra turn is distinct.

A turn normally permits movement, one Action, a Bonus Action when an actual rule grants a use, and one ordinary free object interaction. A second ordinary interaction or an Action-time object activation uses an Action. Brief communication is not an extra Action. Conditions and specific features may restrict these permissions.

The shared limit is one **extra full Action per creature per numbered round**. Such an Action cannot grant another extra Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. This cap is independent of Reaction timing. Extra turns do not by themselves refresh Reactions, recharge, periodic ticks, recovery ticks or the regular-turn allowances defined here.

**Reaction interpretation.** Begin an encounter with one available Reaction unless surprised or otherwise prohibited. Refresh at each regular own-turn start; never at the numbered round boundary or an extra turn. A late-initiative creature can therefore react before its first turn, refresh, and react again in the same numbered round. A legal trigger, available resource and all feature prerequisites are still required.

**Explicit additional Reactions.** A reviewed card can grant a separate limited use without refreshing the ordinary resource. Warrior Mind Shock supplies its stated once-per-duration non-attack Reaction; spending one resource does not consume/reset the other. Surprise, Incapacitated and Focused still restrict both. It grants no Counterspell knowledge or waived costs. Extra turns refresh neither. Per-dose reapplication/stacking and other specific grants remain part of the class semantic pass.

**Surprise — V6 plus NEW Bonus Action clarification.** On a surprised creature's first regular turn it cannot voluntarily move or take an Action or Bonus Action. It cannot react until that turn ends. Its slot, durations, passive effects, concentration, periodic effects and recharge still occur. Surprise alone is not Incapacitated or Unconscious. Brief communication and an otherwise legal simple free interaction remain possible.

**Entry — NEW.** Standard end-round reinforcements roll/receive initiative and first act next round. An explicit midround entrant acts this round only if its complete ordered slot is still upcoming; entry during that exact slot counts as already passed. It has its initial Reaction unless prohibited. A summon-specific timing rule overrides this generic entry procedure.

After the final slot, resolve Core's end-round hazards, reinforcements, morale, objectives and boss phases. Conclude the scene with surrender, capture, pursuit, harvesting access and noise consequences under their own rules; winning initiative does not resolve those automatically.

## Time and event ordering — NEW

For a duration created in initiative, record the relevant original regular start/end marker. Existing effects keep that **virtual marker**, repeating every six seconds if the creature leaves or changes initiative. Reordering, rerolling, extra turns, death/removal or leaving/reentering initiative never restart an existing duration. New effects use the current schedule. Source death still ends concentration, a source-dependent aura/tether or an effect explicitly ending on death.

- A bare hostile target-bound **N rounds** ends at the Nth future regular target-end marker. An in-progress target turn's current end does not count.
- A bare self/source buff, ally-targeted buff or source-controlled aura **N rounds** ends at the Nth future source-start marker. Explicit target-turn, pulse or absolute timing overrides this default. Activation during source turn 1 for three rounds ends at source turn 4's start.
- **Next turn** means the next future regular turn of the named creature, not the current turn's still-upcoming end. An unqualified next turn refers to source/user under the existing shared rule. Explicit “this turn” can include the current turn.
- An outside-initiative bare N-round effect instead gets an absolute application-time + N×6 seconds deadline. Entering initiative preserves that deadline.
- Explicit periodic profiles retain their registered clocks and tick counts. Never create a second timer merely because a generic duration rule also exists.

The [exact GPT review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_COMBAT_EXACT_FINDINGS.md) confirms ally-buff source clocks and excluding the current turn for explicit next-turn endpoints. The helper excludes a specific current-end marker only if that marker would otherwise be selected: application during a turn at time1 with end3 excludes3 and selects9; application at/after3 also selects9, without erroneously skipping again to15.

At a regular turn's **start**, resolve in this order:

1. Expire start-ending effects and apply immediate state changes from those expirations.
2. Refresh Reaction; tick regular-start recharge/non-action clocks.
3. Resolve already-due absolute state recovery if now legal, including a previously blocked Stable recovery deadline.
4. If still alive, dying and at 0 HP with death saves, make that turn's death save.
5. Resolve other start effects and periodic events in application order.
6. Begin voluntary turn decisions.

At **end**, resolve triggered effects, due damage, saves and maintenance before end-ending effects expire; then the slot finishes. No extra turn creates another regular marker. The caller must not reuse a resolved marker.

For simultaneous effects, earlier application timestamp precedes later. For simultaneous components of one source, its printed internal order controls; otherwise use stable application sequence, with source/mechanical ID as a final tie-break. Record that sequence when creating the effects. Beneficial/harmful labels do not change priority. Periodic family arbitration happens once per family/marker before its damage, retaining the family registry's consumed loser ticks.

Examples: dying at 0 rolls its death save before ordinary start-turn healing; a fatal death save is not undone by ordinary healing. Stable at 0 skips the save, then start-turn damage can break Stable. A natural 20 can restore 1 HP before a due Bleed drops it to 0 as a new drop event. If Decay expires while a Stable recovery deadline is already due, the old deadline resolves once without rerolling recovery time.

## Ready

Spend an Action to declare a perceivable trigger and one legal Action-time action or movement. It expires next regular own-turn start. **NEW:** only one pending Ready per creature; replacing it loses the prior setup and any paid held-spell costs. No Bonus Action/Reaction ability, long ritual or multi-minute activity can be prepared by generic Ready.

The trigger happens first, then the readied response immediately follows before later events, unless a specific effect explicitly interrupts. On release spend the normal Reaction and recheck target, range, sight/perception, line of effect, ammunition and other prerequisites. An invalid or declined occurrence spends no release resource; the Ready can wait for another valid occurrence before expiry. This does not undo setup costs. Once released, it is consumed.

For ordinary nonspell actions, feature/ammunition costs are paid on release unless text charges setup. A readied **Attack Action** gets its legally available ordinary attack count; a feature limited to your own turn does not thereby work off-turn. Core Overwatch is explicitly one ranged attack, not that full Attack Action and not Soldier's distinct engine.

A readied spell is actually **cast at preparation**: choose spell/mode, verify legality, pay RP/material/other costs, provide components, resolve Dissonance/Refrain and cast-trigger effects once. Counterspell/cast-interruption opportunity occurs then, not again at release. Every held spell requires concentration, even ordinarily non-concentration spells; incompatible prior concentration ends. Lost concentration loses the held spell and costs. NEW: select the legal target/area point at release and recheck legality without repaying. At release the hold continues as ordinary spell concentration if required, otherwise ends after resolution. Expired/replaced/countered held spells do not refund paid costs.

Ready movement grants a separate current-Speed budget on release, pays terrain costs and can provoke ordinary opportunity attacks. It grants no extra Action, Bonus Action or interaction.

Focused stance's Reaction restriction also blocks an ordinary Ready release; Ready does not create a Counterspell exception. Holding a spell does not waive any current Reaction prohibition.

**Spell-effect duration begins at release.** Its normal duration is anchored when the effect manifests, while Ready expiry and held concentration already run from preparation. A source explicitly tying a particular consequence to casting/preparation retains that consequence's stated clock. No casting cost, Refrain, Dissonance or cast trigger occurs a second time merely from release.

## Stances

Choose one stance during a **regular** own turn before the first event that would use any stance benefit/restriction: attack, spell, relevant check/save or movement. If none occurs, choose before turn end. No retroactive selection. It lasts until next regular start. NEW: extra turns preserve the stance and spent allowances; they cannot choose/replenish it.

| Aggressive | +2 damage once per qualifying weapon attack's damage packet; −2 AC. Not periodic or copied damage. |
| Guarded | +1 AC, advantage on explicit roll/contest resisting Shove, Speed −5 (minimum 0). Its +1 can coexist with Guard's first-attack +2, giving +3 then +1. This combination is explicitly allowed here. |
